chapters.title: Chapter 701: Vexthra’s Worries [Bonus]
paragraphs: After the battle with the BlazeFang Wolf, Kent started to see how slight carelessness or, in his case, overconfidence could cost one’s life.

The domain he was traversing wasn’t as easy as he had thought. It had been five hours since he arrived at Flame Valley and began traversing it, and so far, he had already faced seven flame beasts, each showing him the danger he had found himself in.
He was strong enough to kill them easily, but the survival instinct of the beasts was something he was seeing for the first time.
Kent didn’t even know if this was him being paranoid, but he began to wonder whether his idea of traversing the Flame Valley through the core region was a good idea or a bad one.

However, after every kill, the thrill of facing an even more harrowing beast than the one he had already killed overcame his reasoning, causing him to push forward, even going so far as to wish for more harrowing dangers.
He tried to make sense of where this thrill was coming from, but in the end, he could only conclude that he was crazy.
There was no denying that his craziness was flowing through his blood, so he could only accept himself and resolve that he would move through the thick and thin to get to his destination.

An hour later, Kent met his next target, a stag that wanted to bathe him in flames, but learning from his previous mistakes, he took care of it. A few seconds after killing the stag, Vexthra contacted him through the harem link.
"What are you doing now?"
Kent smiled broadly.
[Are you missing me so badly that you can’t sleep? It is already 9 p.m. here, Vexthra... Get some sleep,]
Vexthra, who was indeed missing the brat, blushed... however, before she could reply, the air around her grew hotter. The next second, she was in Kent’s arms.
"Huh..." The goddess was taken aback, appearing in a domain of fire...
"No need to be alarmed. Welcome to the Flame Valley," Kent said, planting a kiss on her lips. Vexthra was really surprised, but being kissed by Kent helped calm her down.
"So this is what you’re up to," Vexthra asked, looking at the dead stag on the floor. She had already told her sisters she would be away for a few hours.
Being taken away suddenly might have startled them.
"I’m merely moving toward my destination; this place happens to be in my path," Kent replied, hovering in the air with Vexthra in his arms.
"I’m 100% sure you could have gone around it and gotten to your destination much faster," Vexthra smirked, knowing she was right.
It didn’t take a genius to know the brat was making his own life difficult by traversing the vast expanse of scorching land.
Kent grinned, looking closely at Vexthra. "I happen to need flame spirits, so I might as well hunt for some on my way to my destination."
Vexthra couldn’t deny Kent’s reasoning, considering she would have done the same thing too if she were in Kent’s place.
The place is where most adventurers harvest flame spirit and sell to the alchemist at exaggerated prices, so instead of buying, which he could have, he wanted to get his own.
"What’s going on with your exploration of the Four Floating Islands?" Kent asked.
"We found some battle styles on the third island, and thanks to Unity, they’re learning it—well, the ones using bow, spear, and swords are learning it since it was meant for them...
And oh... Unity can now use the sword... crazy, right?" Vexthra said with a beaming smile.
Kent just smiled.

He had already experienced what it felt like to start recovering memories of his past life. So he was happy for Unity, knowing that this was all because of what Chaos had done during the Primordial Era.
Hearing that one of his wives was benefiting from it made him feel a sense of fulfillment.
His only concern is what all this ultimately means. Something this grand means the price might also be huge, so he worries about that. But for now, he is happy...
"Good thing Unity is improving. I’m sure soon they will all start to adapt to the changes, especially knowing they had past lives and that their memories from those past lives will begin to surface."
Vexthra looked at Kent and nodded slightly. Kent smiled, planting a kiss on her lips.

"How about you? Are you prepared for what the past will reveal?" Kent asked, and Vexthra sighed. She would be lying if she said she wasn’t already looking forward to the day she would see a glimpse of the past.
She was indeed looking forward to that.

Her only worry now was whether learning about her past would change her current self for the worse. A few years ago, she was the embodiment of hate until she met Kent. The brat helped her understand what empathy, love, and other emotions feel like.
Then she met her sisters, and things turned even better for her. Now, she had learned her past memories could be retrieved using a key.
But she was worried that the moment those memories came back, she would revert to her former, resentful self.

Kent tightened his hold on her when he heard her answer to his question. He kissed her neck and, with a whisper, assured her, "No need to worry about something like that, Vex... Memories aren’t that scary... unless your past self was a crazy, psychotic, lunatic bastard who seemed to find joy in torturing you."
"Are we still talking about me?" Vexthra asked, smiling. She could tell Kent was talking about himself, and from the look of things, Kent and his past self seemed to be having a problem.
This caused the amusing smile on her face to spread. Of course, that was what Kent wanted to see. He knew better than anyone how crazy past lives can be.
But even as crazy as Chaos was to him, he wasn’t affected in any bad way. If anything, he had made significant progress thanks to Chaos.
So, Vexthra would be fine.
They spent a couple of hours discussing additional topics, which mostly involved Kent asking numerous questions about elemental cultivation. Then, he sent Vexthra away.
Kent spent a few moments analyzing how best to help his ladies when they start unlocking their memories.
"I guess when things start happening, I will know what to do." Kent started moving deeper into the domain of fire, killing the flame beasts he encountered on the way...

chapters.title: Chapter 702: Fire Seraphim Beetle
paragraphs: "Fuck, this is not how I expected my day to go," Kent muttered, looking around him. Bodies of beasts he had slain lay strewn on the ground.

He had just stepped into the inner section of the Flame Valley, yet the danger he found himself in wasn’t one he expected. Of course, he dealt with it, but the energy expended in the battles was much more than he used for the other flame beast he killed in the outer section.
The last beast he took down was the same as the first beast he killed when he stepped into the Flame Valley. But this one had already reached the Core Formation and had refined its core three times.
Of course, its bloodline remained unawakened, but it was already too dangerous to be underestimated. So Kent took the battle seriously.
Thankfully, he wasn’t some weak, overconfident brat who chose to throw his life away. Kent has the strength to back up his arrogance, so he used it to continue moving forward.
Still, he hadn’t yet found a single beast with flame spirits. But regardless of that setback, he was moving, and slowly he neared the edge of the Core area.
His resistance was still coming along, but not enough to take him to the first stage in Flame Resistance cultivation.
Thankfully, the heat was even more scorching in the inner section, and as he neared the core, he could sense that he was about to enter a different level of hotness.
"Wow, damn..." Kent moved to his right and rolled on the ground, evading a piercing attack. The attack struck the ground, creating a loud explosion that sent a shockwave in every direction.
Before Kent could recover, another attack came from an unknown direction. It just zipped through the air, aiming to pierce a hole through Kent’s forehead.
However, he dodged again and spread his senses. That was when Kent saw who was attacking him...
"A beetle."

It was a large beetle with iridescent fiery wings and a glowing horn. The horns mounted on its head were where the attacks came from, and judging by how fast the attacks were coming, it was clear Kent had met a real challenger this time.
He quickly scanned it...
⟦Name: Fire Seraphim Beetle⟧
⟦Bloodline: None⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (6/7)⟧
⟦Flame Spirit: Blaze Wisp⟧
"Interesting... I will be getting my first flame spirit," Kent smiled cheerfully as he prepared for battle.
Kent retrieved his sword, and sword qi swirled around it while the air was thick with sword intent. Kent knew he had found himself in a sticky one.
Right when his sword appeared, a thick shade fell on Kent. Up ahead, a giant beetle with 20-meter-wide wings appeared, lunging at Kent.
Kent quickly distanced himself by blinking away. However, the beetle didn’t abandon the attack. Instead, it landed heavily on the ground, causing it to shake.
Then, from the shock, a powerful explosion erupted from the ground, shooting lava at Kent.
Sword qi surged from Kent’s blade, cutting through the thick, scorching lava as he retaliated with a swift slash aimed at the beetle’s wings.
The wings were large, so it was an obvious target. However, Kent was shocked when his attack was evaded.

The beetle twisted midair, narrowly avoiding the blow, but Kent saw a faint scorch mark trail behind. The beetle screeched—a terrifying sound that echoed through the valley—before charging again with relentless fury.
Kent leapt backward, narrowly escaping a deadly thrust. The ground beneath him cracked and smoldered from the heat of the attack.
Landing on the ground, Kent unleashed a ’Doom Shard’ from the ground, sending it through the wings of the beetle. This attack worked, causing the creature to falter midair.
However, to Kent’s shock, his next attack struck the beetle, but it dispersed into nothingness.
’Illusion.’ Kent wondered, watching his Doom shard move through the air before it vanished.
Of course, it wasn’t a real illusion per se, but the beetle was able to use visual distortions to deceive Kent...
The attack struck an illusion while the main beetle was already upon Kent. He used ’Blink’ to distance himself, buying a second to ponder what had just happened.
"I have enough mental strength to see through illusion... so why couldn’t I see through the beetle’s illusion?"

⟦That was because the Fire Seraphim Beetle has the Blaze Wisp flame. It possesses properties that allow it to distort space, creating an illusion of fire energy in the air. You failed to see it because of the high concentration of fire energy in the air.⟧

"That makes sense," Kent muttered and then blinked away again. A large quantity of flame energy will indeed cause such an illusion to be missed by Kent. He was basically in the Beatles’ domain after all...
Kent readied his attacks and went into battle again.
This time, he unleashed the ’Rapid Slash’ skill, sending 450 sword arcs into the beetle. It managed to evade a few, but some landed on its injured wings, causing it to falter yet again.
This gave Kent the best opportunity to attack, and he seized it. His sword flashed forward just one time, but dozens of sword lights flashed out, landing on the other wing of the beetle.
The moment those attacks connected, the beetle lost control of its flight and landed heavily on the ground. Thankfully, when it comes to killing things on the ground, Kent has the best skill.
Dozens of doom shards emerged from the ground, piercing the giant body of the beetle. That was enough to kill it.
The doom shard skill had already become much stronger, so it would have killed the beetle even if Kent used just one.
The moment the beetle died, the flame spirit emerged from the horn protruding from its head.
Kent moved toward it in an attempt to retrieve it. But as he got closer, his senses started to falter. "So that is how it is," Kent became intrigued. He quickly approached and retrieved it.
⟦Name: Blaze Wisp⟧
⟦Grade: Heaven⟧
⟦Beast Flame Chart: 6075⟧
⟦Effect: Grants enhanced fire resistance and the ability to create fire illusions.⟧
"Tower, what is this beast Flame Chart?" Kent asked, noticing the new addition when he appraised the spirit flame.
⟦The Beast Flame Chart is a universal ranking set to determine the most powerful beast flames in existence. The one you have just obtained is ranked 6075... Very weak.⟧
"You don’t have to tell me, Tower, I know it is weak," Kent smiled and then chose to devour the Blaze Wisp spirit flame...

chapters.title: Chapter 703: Weak Flame Resistance
paragraphs: ⟦Your Soul Flame has devoured a Spirit Flame: Blaze Wisp⟧
⟦Your Soul Flame Grows Stronger⟧
The chaos flame devoured the "Blaze Wisp" flame as if it were a spoonful of dinner. It happened so easily that Kent only felt his soul flame grow stronger for a second, and that was all.

"I need to add more if I want to increase the quality to Tier 7. I need to get to Tier 7 before I can concoct Tier 9 pills, and that should happen much faster if I want to have a shot at defeating the Pill Princess."
Kent smiled and then decided to go deeper into the Flame Valley’s core region. The danger started to show as he moved deeper.
If anyone were to find out that Kent was roaming freely in the core region of the Flame Valley, they would probably claw their faces raw, peeling every layer of skin off in utter disbelief.
Such recklessness was unheard of—no one dared tread that scorching inferno without overwhelming strength or a death wish.
The sheer shock that would riddle them would be too much for their minds to comprehend, shattering their sense of reality and making their hearts pound with terror.
They would probably end up fearing Kent.
Why that?

Because before anyone dared traverse the scorching expanse of land, they had to come in teams. Teams of able and capable warriors dared to venture into the core region of the Flame Valley, not a single human.

But even with a team, not all managed to come back alive. That is how harrowing the core region of the Flame Valley is, and because of that, if they found out Kent was alone and freely walking through the domain of fire, they would probably picture him as a devil.
The heat alone is something that many had to invest millions of spirit stones in flame resistance pills before they dared enter the scorching depths of the Flame Valley.

However, the Chaos Dragon was moving even deeper into the core region, which, if he managed to cross, would put him inside the inner area on the other side and eventually find himself in the outer section, where he could continue his journey.
The next beast Kent faced was a "Burning Mantis." It was a rather beautiful creature that would have been left alone to wander the vast scorched valley, but it attacked first, so Kent killed it.
He didn’t gain a flame spirit from it, but it dropped a core filled with flame energy.
It was the first time Kent came across a beast dropping a core, so he quickly absorbed it. Right then, he felt the change.
⟦You have absorbed a large amount of Fire Energy⟧
⟦You have attained Weak Flame Resistance⟧

"Looks like attaining weak resistance to flame has already made me immune to the heat in this region..." Kent smiled. "I never knew a weak resistance was all it would take to feel at home here... Looks like this valley is not that dangerous."
With this new resolve, Kent started moving deeper into the core region, looking for the next beast to kill and the next flame spirit to devour...

However, even after moving for several hours and killing dozens of Flame Beasts, he never acquired a single flame spirit. However, he gained two more cores, which provided a boost to his fire resistance.
Not that he needed to resist anything...
Of course, aside from gaining two more cores, he also discovered that his resistance to attacks from flame skills had improved slightly.
Aside from resisting harmful attacks, he essentially allowed the weaker ones to land on him, gradually building his resistance.
Eventually, he started allowing the stronger attacks to land on him. Though it hurt like hell, he saw a boost in both his body cultivation and flame resistance, so he couldn’t complain.
Eventually, Kent met his next target, one who had a flame spirit.
⟦Name: Cinderback Rhino⟧
⟦Bloodline: None⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (7/7)⟧
⟦Flame Spirit: Pyre Sprite⟧
It was a welcome message to Kent, so he faced the brute flame beast that came, shaking the very ground it ran on. Unlike the Beetle, this one couldn’t fly, so the battle was grounded.

It took just five minutes, but by the end, the two-mile radius was destroyed beyond repair. Kent tried to handle most of the attacks defenseless, but it was a failed attempt, for he never had the heart to stand against a moving truck of pure stone muscle slamming into him.
Kent had to distance himself three kilometers before the Void Cleave was able to penetrate the body of the beast. It was one tough bastard that wouldn’t just die.

Of course, Kent didn’t use too much force, as he was learning to wield his skills with minimal effort. He wanted to gain a much deeper understanding of them, since, aside from attaining seven-sword enlightenment, he must also lay the foundation for the three-sword moves.

So while using techniques like the "Nine Calamities Sword Strike" could have killed any of the beasts he faced easily, he focused more on combat experience and understanding, which in the long run will come in handy.
After getting the flame spirit, Kent fed it to the Chaos Flame, which became much more powerful; however, it still hadn’t reached the sixth Tier.
But Kent pressed on and eventually came across another beast...
This time it was a "Firemane Lion," one terrifying beast. But it took Kent a minute to handle it. Then, from there, he began to follow the path that led deeper into the core region.
The Chaos Flame was almost at the Tier 6 stage, so Kent was pushing to at least get there before his time to leave the Valley arrived.
He had spent over a day there already, meaning he had less than two days to get to the Half-Elf Kingdom. He wanted to arrive a day early so he could get accustomed to the place before venturing out.
Eventually, Kent came across another beast, and after defeating it, he fed the spirit flame to his Soul Flame. He finally managed to raise his soul flame to Tier 6...
⟦Your Soul Flame has devoured a Spirit Flame: Flare Ghost⟧
⟦The Quality of your Soul Flame has been upgraded from Tier 5 ↠ Tier 6⟧
"I have stayed here long enough, so I guess it is time to leave..." Kent sighed, "I will come back later for more."

Because before anyone dared traverse the scorching expanse of land, they had to come in teams.
Teams of able and capable warriors dared to venture into the core region of the Flame Valley, not a single human.
But even with a team, not all managed to come back alive.

That is how harrowing the core region of the Flame Valley is, and because of that, if they found out Kent was alone and freely walking through the domain of fire, they would probably picture him as a devil.
The heat alone is something that many had to invest millions of spirit stones in flame resistance pills before they dared enter the scorching depths of the Flame Valley.

However, the Chaos Dragon was moving even deeper into the core region, which, if he managed to cross, would put him inside the inner area on the other side and eventually find himself in the outer section, where he could continue his journey.
The next beast Kent faced was a "Burning Mantis." It was a rather beautiful creature that would have been left alone to wander the vast scorched valley, but it attacked first, so Kent killed it.
He didn’t gain a flame spirit from it, but it dropped a core filled with flame energy.
It was the first time Kent came across a beast dropping a core, so he quickly absorbed it.
Right then, he felt the change.
⟦You have absorbed a large amount of Fire Energy⟧
⟦You have attained Weak Flame Resistance⟧
"Looks like attaining weak resistance to flame has already made me immune to the heat in this region..." Kent smiled.
"I never knew a weak resistance was all it would take to feel at home here...
Looks like this valley is not that dangerous."
With this new resolve, Kent started moving deeper into the core region, looking for the next beast to kill and the next flame spirit to devour...
However, even after moving for several hours and killing dozens of Flame Beasts, he never acquired a single flame spirit.
However, he gained two more cores, which provided a boost to his fire resistance.
Not that he needed to resist anything...
Of course, aside from gaining two more cores, he also discovered that his resistance to attacks from flame skills had improved slightly.
Aside from resisting harmful attacks, he essentially allowed the weaker ones to land on him, gradually building his resistance.
Eventually, he started allowing the stronger attacks to land on him.
Though it hurt like hell, he saw a boost in both his body cultivation and flame resistance, so he couldn’t complain.
Eventually, Kent met his next target, one who had a flame spirit.
⟦Name: Cinderback Rhino⟧
⟦Bloodline: None⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (7/7)⟧
⟦Flame Spirit: Pyre Sprite⟧
It was a welcome message to Kent, so he faced the brute flame beast that came, shaking the very ground it ran on.
Unlike the Beetle, this one couldn’t fly, so the battle was grounded.
It took just five minutes, but by the end, the two-mile radius was destroyed beyond repair.
Kent tried to handle most of the attacks defenseless, but it was a failed attempt, for he never had the heart to stand against a moving truck of pure stone muscle slamming into him.
Kent had to distance himself three kilometers before the Void Cleave was able to penetrate the body of the beast.
It was one tough bastard that wouldn’t just die.
Of course, Kent didn’t use too much force, as he was learning to wield his skills with minimal effort.
He wanted to gain a much deeper understanding of them, since, aside from attaining seven-sword enlightenment, he must also lay the foundation for the three-sword moves.

So while using techniques like the "Nine Calamities Sword Strike" could have killed any of the beasts he faced easily, he focused more on combat experience and understanding, which in the long run will come in handy.
After getting the flame spirit, Kent fed it to the Chaos Flame, which became much more powerful; however, it still hadn’t reached the sixth Tier.
But Kent pressed on and eventually came across another beast...
This time it was a "Firemane Lion," one terrifying beast.
But it took Kent a minute to handle it.
Then, from there, he began to follow the path that led deeper into the core region.
The Chaos Flame was almost at the Tier 6 stage, so Kent was pushing to at least get there before his time to leave the Valley arrived.
He had spent over a day there already, meaning he had less than two days to get to the Half-Elf Kingdom.
He wanted to arrive a day early so he could get accustomed to the place before venturing out.
Eventually, Kent came across another beast, and after defeating it, he fed the spirit flame to his Soul Flame.
He finally managed to raise his soul flame to Tier 6...
⟦Your Soul Flame has devoured a Spirit Flame: Flare Ghost⟧
⟦The Quality of your Soul Flame has been upgraded from Tier 5 ↠ Tier 6⟧
"I have stayed here long enough, so I guess it is time to leave..." Kent sighed, "I will come back later for more."

chapters.title: Chapter 704: First Contact [Bonus]
paragraphs: After the Chaos Flame reached Tier 6, Kent decided to leave. His aim was Tier 7, but it would take some time before he could get enough spirit flames to upgrade his flame.
This meant that if he wanted to first reach Tier 7 before leaving, he might be too late to get to Elarion.
So he placed a pin in his hunting now, knowing he would come back soon enough to continue his hunt. For now, getting back to his mission was the priority.
Kent started carving his way through the Valley. On his way, he encountered some dangerous flame-type beasts, even managing to kill one that possessed a spirit flame.

Kent managed to get his soul flame stronger yet again while he moved through the core section of the valley. The Flame Valley is vast and filled with danger, but since he wasn’t there to hunt to his heart’s content, his movement was in a straight line.
But that was enough to get him some spirit flames. The next Tier would be determined based on how long he would be staying in the domain of fire.

"Looks like I have reached the inner section on the other side." After three hours of moving, Kent came to a stop when he felt the air lose considerable heat. It was easy to determine he had left the core region.

"So I have to move toward the right side of the Northern region, which will take me to Elarion." After making up his mind, Kent started moving yet again, this time toward the kingdom of the Half-Elves.
Meanwhile, somewhere in the inner section of Flame Valley, where Kent was currently located, three Half-Elves were engaged in a life-or-death battle with a Core Formation-stage flame beast.

The beast was a hideous-looking spider with long metallic legs and glowing red skin. Its eyes burned with furious energy. And judging by the green flame around it, the spider clearly had a flame spirit.
"Cyran, circle around it and don’t let the flame touch you; it is poisonous... aim for its eyes." A dark-haired half-elf wielding a spear shouted, commanding his teammate on what to do.

Cyran, a blonde, handsome half-elf, did as he was told, moving across the battlefield as he aimed his arrows at the eyes of the spider, just like he was told. However, no matter how hard he tried, he just couldn’t get an arrow through.
"Arion, I don’t think we can get through its defense. This beast looks like it has the skin of metal," Cyran said, frustration evident in his eyes.

Arion, the dark-haired spearman, stabbed his spear into the ground, raising the very earth the spider stood on, trying to knock it to the side, but the spider easily evaded, rendering the attack useless.
But it wasn’t for nothing. The moment the spider landed on the ground, the ground gave way, and four of its legs started to sink into the earth.
The moment they entered, the ground hardened, trapping the four legs... but it can be trapped only for a second, considering the hardening wasn’t strong enough to make a difference.
However, it was long enough for the third teammate, a dark-haired young lady, to cast a spell, manifesting a thick bolt of lightning that descended on the spider, landing square on its back.
The bolt knocked the spider off its many feet, giving Cyran the shot he had been waiting for. An arrow appeared on his bow, and with a quick pull, the arrow left the string.
It was a good shot; however, it didn’t reach the spider. Just when the spider was about to lose one eye—a wound that would have cost it its life—a different beast arrived, deflecting the arrow.
"What... the Blistering Ant." Arion, the leader of the team, recognized the new arrival, causing his eyes to widen.

"Helyra, what’s up?" Before Arion could respond, he heard Cyran shout at their female mage teammate. Thankfully, Helyra’s reaction speed was quick enough, and she evaded an attack from the third beast, a Firetail Scorpion.
"Firetail Scorpion." The grim look on Cyran’s face gave way to fear.
Three of the most powerful beasts within the inner region of the Flame Valley now surrounded them on three sides, and the more harrowing thing was that the three were allies.

Inside the Flame Region, most beasts team up if they want to have a shot at survival. These flame beasts may be more like monsters, lacking sentience like most beastkin, but when it comes to survival, they know best.
So, they are a team; they hunt together, and now they have caught three mortals within an inescapable ring.

The Blistering Ant was a giant ant with a fiery stinger and a hardened, heat-resistant shell. It looked even more terrifying than the spider. Black flames surrounded its body, indicating it also possessed a spirit flame.
The Firetail Scorpion also has a red flame surrounding its body, indicating that it possesses a spirit flame as well. It had a rather large and long tail ignited in flames as it eyed Helyra.
Cyran was also locked in a stare-down with the spider, while Arion found himself gazing into the deadly eyes of the Blistering Ant.

All three half-elves wore fearful expressions because, despite being at the Core Formation stage, the three beasts had already refined their cores five times, while Cyran and Helyra refined theirs once, and Arion twice.
The gap in strength was just too wide to handle such monstrosities on their own. If anything, they should be running now. However, escaping would be hard...

The three beasts created a net around the three half-elves. This was their hunting strategy, and it had worked not once, but dozens of times. Today, too, they were about to feast on the bodies of the three half-elves.
"Arion, what should we do?" Helyra asked, tears falling down her cheeks. "I don’t want to die... I can’t die just yet." It was plain that her death would destroy many who were waiting for her return.

Arion, the leader of the team, tightened his grip on his spear. He didn’t want to die either—not when he still had more years to live. But as it turned out, fighting four realms above them wasn’t plausible—not at their level.
All hope was lost, and they were aware of it. But they didn’t want to die. However, just as their souls were about to give up on them, a lazy voice entered their ears.
"Do you guys need help?"

chapters.title: Chapter 705: Making Friends [Bonus]
paragraphs: If it weren’t for the precarious situation the three Half-Elves found themselves in, their answer to Kent’s question would have been, "Are you kidding us? We fucking need saving right now."

But they don’t have that luxury, considering the monsters around them could move at any moment if they talked. And while it sounded like a person’s voice, they didn’t know if their ears were playing tricks on them.

So while Kent’s voice did little to cheer them on, it wasn’t until they saw him walking toward the scorpion as if it were some bug that they knew it wasn’t that their ears were deceiving them, someone actually asked the question.
When they saw how Kent was strolling toward the scorpion, one hand in his pocket and the other holding a few grapes, they were both shocked.
However, they knew they had to seek help first...
"Please save us, and we will give you all we have," Arion spoke in a desperate tone. However, the next second, Helyra shouted, "Watch out!"
The spider stabbed its leg at Arion’s head. It was a quick and decisive strike, one aimed to kill just when hope seemed to be around the corner.
All three Half-Elves closed their eyes, not wanting to see one of them die, and the other not wanting to see the pain in the eyes of his friends as he passed.
However, after three seconds, when none had died, they slowly opened their eyes only to see three dead beasts, killed with a thick black spear.
The spear was about 5 meters tall and 13 inches thick.
It was the updated version of the Doom Shard. It was still a Mythic-grade skill, but Kent had upgraded the rank from SSS to SSS+.
This gave it a new name: Doom Spear.
Kent was bored as he made his way out of the Valley, so he decided to use his millions of skill upgrade points to upgrade that skill. He never knew it would become this deadly.
The three Half-Elves had to look at the bodies of the three beasts for a few minutes before they managed to register that they were dead.
They then turned, looking at Kent with wide eyes. The brat, of course, smiled... "You can call me Kent... Kent Madson."

The Half-Elves were so shocked that they didn’t know what to say. Eventually, they managed to calm down. Arion walked toward Kent, and when he was a few steps away, his eyes landed on Kent’s ear, causing him to stop.
"You are a human," Arion said, prompting his friends to stare at Kent’s ear.
"Yes. I am a human from the human continent. Nice meeting you." The three Half-Elves were taken aback, but then they recovered. They are Half-Elves, meaning they are half-human, half-Elf.
In a way, they are just hybrid humans. So, it wasn’t too hard to accept the fact that a human being was standing before them.
"Nice meeting you, too. I am Arion, this is Cyrus, and Helyra." Arion shook Kent’s hand.
"Thank you for saving us," Arion said, and his friends nodded. They were truly grateful.

"Please, if you don’t take your flame spirits, they will disappear." Arion turned toward the spirit flames that appeared on all three beasts. If he had the means, he would have grabbed it, but he had to give it to the owner.
After all, Kent killed the three Beasts.
Kent turned and looked at the spirit flames. After a quick scan, a sigh escaped his lips. "You guys can have the ones on the spider and ant... I will take the scorpion."
"WHAT?"
"Are you sure?" Arion and his friends asked in shocked tones.
"Yeah. I only need this one." Kent walked toward the scorpion’s body, leaving the three friends to stare at his back with expressions of shock.
Even tears began to fall from Helyra’s eyes when she saw that Kent didn’t want the two flames, meaning they were now theirs to have.
Her tears flowed freely.
This was because one spirit flame, regardless of its grade, sells for millions of spirit stones... and to people like them, a million spirit stones is something they could only dream of.

They were just a team of three who wanted to make a living for themselves and their families. So far, they had only managed to get a flame core from a Root Sovereign beast and three beast bodies, which they planned to sell for a couple of thousand spirit stones.

But now, they were not only getting two spirit flames—something they had never obtained before—but they would also be walking home with two heaven-grade spirit flames. That was worth several million spirit stones.
"What are you three doing? If you don’t take the flames, they will vanish." Kent’s voice snapped them out of their dazed state.
He was indeed aware of spirit flames, but the two wouldn’t have much effect on his Chaos flame.
When his soul flame reached Tier 6, he sensed that the flame yearned for something stronger. The two flames on the spider and ant ranked 10,008 and 10,809 on the Beast Flame Chart.
Those were just too weak for him, so he might as well give them to the Half-Elves. They clearly needed them more than he did.
The three nodded and retrieved the spirit flames, their expressions shocked yet happy.
"How about the bodies?" Arion asked.

"If they have a core, then I want that, but aside from that, you can have the bodies too." Now that his ladies were fighting real beasts in the dungeon, he didn’t need weaker bodies like these to create undead.

"You can have this." Helyra quickly removed the core and handed it to Kent, who received it with a happy expression. The more cores he absorbed, the stronger his flame resistance grew. Additionally, he began to sense that his control over the flame had reached a new level.
This meant his alchemy skills would rise much higher the next time he sat down to concoct pills. So he received the core and absorbed it.
"Please, where are you going?" Cyrus asked.
"Elarion," Kent answered, and from the look on the faces of the three Half-Elves he had saved, he saw what they wanted to say.
"We are going back now, so if you don’t mind, you can go with us," Arion said, and Kent nodded.
"That would be great." The three Half-Elves smiled and stored away the beast bodies. Kent smiled, watching their happy expressions.
’If I had known, I would have taken the bodies of all the beasts I killed, but it was already too late now.’

chapters.title: Chapter 706: Adventurers [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent, Arion, Cyran, and Helyra quickly left the battleground and began heading out of the inner area, back to the outer section, and ultimately, back to Elarion.

Of course, Arion and his friends tried to take Kent through the safest path known to all who hunted in the Flame Region. However, upon examining the map, Kent realized it would take much longer, so he chose the shortest route to traverse.
They protested that the path he had chosen would be fraught with danger, but after Kent handled the first beast they encountered, they began following him as if he were their leader.
After a while, they arrived in the outer region...
"That was intense," Cyran said, taking a deep breath. Kent turned and looked at him, smiling.
"So you three are like some adventurers who pick quests and complete them?" Kent asked.

"No... We don’t qualify as adventurers since we haven’t yet obtained the adventurer’s qualification. But this time, after this sale, we will get our dreams fulfilled..." Arion said with a happy expression.
Cyran and Helyra were also happy. They were part of the nobodies in the Half-Elves region, despite being Core Formation experts. They were basically at the bottom of the well, which was shocking.

The strongest in the human world were at the 4th level of the Core Formation stage two years ago, and even to date, Kent knew, aside from perhaps the hidden expert whom most chose to live in the ancient battlefield of Parting, the three standing before him had the strength to bring the humans to their knees.
Yet as it stood, such people were not even regarded as qualified candidates to join the adventurers’ guild. That baffled Kent slightly.
"How exactly do things work in this part of the world?" Kent asked. "I mean, for powerful warriors like you three, joining the adventurers’ guild shouldn’t be too hard, right?"
Arion smiled, shaking his head. "We may be at the Core Formation stage, but to join the adventurers’ guild, you have to meet some requirements.
The first is to have three or more people in your team. A lone individual can’t become an adventurer, so you need a team. We already met that requirement.
The second is to be at the Core Formation stage, and at least refine your core once. We qualify for that, too.

The third and last requirement is where we have been stuck for the past 17 years since this team was formed. To become an adventurer, we were to kill a Beast possessing a spirit flame and present both the flame and the beast at the adventurers’ guild.
We have been trying for years now, but despite killing quite a sizable number of beasts, we have never had much luck getting a spirit flame from any of them—until now.
"So, thank you for helping us realize our dream," Arion explained, and Kent nodded. The requirements truly explain why they were grateful when he let them have the two spirit flames.

Is becoming an adventurer worth more than your lives? Sorry if I am rude, but I just don’t understand," Kent asked, wearing a questioning expression.

Kent nodded with a smile. "I can’t argue that. That man was wise for sure... Fighting for your family is noble, and it’s what drives all of us to wake up every day and grind."
Kent was impressed by their drive. What motivated them every day was their desire to leave their families in good standing.

"Tell me more about the Elves... everything you know about them that suggests why they hate humans."

chapters.title: Chapter 707: Complex Relationship
paragraphs: "The animosity between the Elves and the humans, as far as I know, started a long time ago... even before the Battle of the Parting. But it intensified about 100 years ago," Helyra began. "From what I know, long before the parting, the humans were allies with the Elves.
I learned that the humans back then were powerful life magicians, and since most Elves are also life magicians, they became close.

I don’t know much, but I know the humans and the Elves had a falling out over something—some say it was an Ascension platform, while others say it was a rare treasure they discovered in some ancient ruin. However, after that event, the humans and the Elves became enemies.
Now, they don’t see eye to eye, and so if you had come through the Elf Kingdom, I had a feeling they would have attacked you."
Kent just nodded, taking Helyra’s words in. It wasn’t like he had any plans to mend the relationship between humans and elves.

He merely wanted to know, and from what he had just heard, the humans and the Elves would never be friends ever again. This kind of breakup, without public knowledge of the root cause, often turns out to be a difficult one.

The cause, when discovered, mostly revolved around a great betrayal, and that was something Kent had no interest in. He just came to get what he wanted. If humans and Elves don’t talk forever, then they can remain enemies.
Helyra talked more, but everything wasn’t something Kent could rely too heavily on, so he just listened and absorbed them as they came.
"Thank you, Helyra," Kent said, walking out of the Outer section of the Flame Valley. Helyra nodded with a pleased expression.

"So, how did you cross the Black Sea? I learned that there is a guardian who knows when someone is passing or can tell when someone is passing. Did you encounter this guardian?" Arion asked with a skeptical expression.
"I did meet a guardian, but one thing led to another, and we became friends. So he allowed me to pass," Kent smiled. "He is an amazing person, by the way... he was fun to be around."

The three Half-Elves looked at each other and began to wonder how such a thing was possible. They heard stories of this sea guardian, so hearing Kent speak casually about him made them wonder many things.
However, after a few seconds, they could only sigh.
"If the Elves know there is a human roaming these areas, they will be pissed," Cyran said with a chuckle.
"Those bastards, all they know is how to do this and that to make the lives of others much more painful."
"I only pray this time, the people from our side get to enter the Supreme Immortal Sect," Arion added, causing Kent to ask a question.
Of course, Shax already told him what was happening, but hearing from them would be much more beneficial.
"Is something happening in your kingdom?" Kent asked.
"Yes," Arion answered. "The Flame Tower will be opening in three weeks, where geniuses from all over the world will enter to comprehend flame techniques.
Those who manage to comprehend a technique to some stage will have a chance to enter the Supreme Immortal Sect and become a disciple if they pass their exams."
"Tell me more."
"Very well. The Supreme Immortal Sect is the largest and strongest sect in the entire world. It is the place where the best of the best are sent.
Rumor has it they have the means to even go to other medium-level worlds and compete in competitions, explore runes, and many more.
Some rumors say they have access to even more rewarding yet dangerous places than the Ancient Battlefield of Parting, where they send their disciples to train and hunt for treasures.
So many rumors about them, but one thing is sure: they are indeed the place to become the best of the best. Even outer-area disciples from there can enter the core section of the Flame Valley."
Kent raised his brow.
"I even learned that some core disciples from the Supreme Immortal Sect had already ascended after passing a test.
That sect is a place where they create monsters, and while I, or any of us, don’t have the talent to enter that place, many who possess some qualifications want to join.
Entering the Flame Tower marks the beginning for them. Of course, there are other ways to enter the Supreme Immortal Sect... but the easiest is the Flame Tower.
Initially, it was based on selection, but this time the King wants to hold an open competition to select the top five to enter the Flame Tower, which is opening in three weeks."
"Then, if it is open, why won’t you three enter?" Kent asked.

"We don’t have the flame element, which is a major requirement before you can register your name. However, even if we did possess the fire element and somehow entered the top five, we couldn’t simply enter the Flame Tower and expect to gain entry to the Supreme Immortal Sect as well.

They only select those at the core formation stage, and the age is below 100. We are older than a hundred years, so we can’t even start to think we have a future if we want to enter such a world of geniuses."
The three shook their heads with weak smiles.
"Don’t look down on yourselves," Kent said as a word of encouragement. At least learning something new about this world was a bonus to him.
He had already been to a high world and the Flame Valley, and so far, he had started to see some changes. First, the Flame Valley was a dangerous place.

Most of the Flame beasts he killed were dangerous. Ordinary warriors would have fallen, but he had just learned that Outer Disciples from the Supreme Immortal Sect can enter the Core area of the Flame Valley.
This means that the Inner and Core disciples will be among the most powerful warriors in the world.
Kent compared them to Fedora and knew that such a high world didn’t live up to its name. He expected dangerous beings, but they were above average in his opinion.

Of course, Vexthra told him high worlds are dangerous, but also said Fedora is one of the weakest. This then means it isn’t about the world; it was more about the dangers surrounding it that push one to seek more strength.
The Foxkins are seeking more strength, which one day will make them much more dangerous than they are now.

Additionally, within the Flame Valley, the beasts had to adapt to survive, becoming equally dangerous. The same principle applied to the Ancient Battlefield of Parting; those roaming there continued to grow stronger.
Now, he knew the Supreme Immortal Sect was the same; only the best survive, and he intended to get in and see what he could gain from there.

chapters.title: Chapter 708: Desire
paragraphs: "You didn’t tell us why you are here. The humans who came to this side of the continent either had dealings with the demons or wanted to sell stuff to use. They always come through the demon gate in the Ancient Battlefield of Parting.
However, as for the last time a human came here, I don’t recall when. So why are you here?" Cyran asked.
Kent had already been made aware of how the other continents treat humans.
Of course, Shax told him if he wanted to stay much longer, then the Half-Elves would be the most welcoming...
Of course, while humans are weak, that was why they were suppressed; Kent never expected to find out that this world isn’t as weak as he had expected.
This made him want to explore it as a human being, regardless of what anyone thought of humans.

So while he waits for the Hand to get their affairs in order, he will find something to keep him going... and since he also needed to defeat the Pill Princess, he had to stay longer and get into the Supreme Immortal Sect.

"Actually, I am here to see if I can get into the Supreme Immortal Sect. Naturally, I would have joined from the human continent, but since the Supreme Immortal Sect doesn’t see the humans as worthy candidates, the only path is to join a different race and try my luck..."
"So you plan on joining the Half-Elves?" Arion asked.
"That is the plan. I don’t know if it would work, but I will try my luck there."
The three didn’t say anything but chose to ponder what Kent had said. They would be lying if they said Kent doesn’t have what it takes to have a shot at joining the Supreme Immortal Sect.
They came across a few disciples from that sect and, knowing what they saw following Kent, they recognized his talent, which qualified him to be a disciple there.
The only question now, however, was whether the Half-Elves would allow a human to take a spot to enter the Flame Tower.
They just don’t see that happening. It almost felt like Kent wasn’t ideal to represent them. However, he can be a good seed that they can rely on to give a resounding slap to the Elves.
"I have a question," Helyra asked, her tone sounding like she needed clarification on something. "Are you below 100 years old?

This is a cultivation world where people can disguise themselves, masking their age. However, to qualify for a slot to join the Flame Tower, you must have the Flame Element, be below 100 years, and be at the core formation stage.
You have to know that it’s an open competition, but the ultimate goal is to gain entry into the Supreme Immortal Sect, so do you qualify for all of them?
And before you ask, the answer is yes... if you fake your age, they will know, so be sure not to do that."
Kent smiled and lit his Chaos Flame. "As you can see, I have a Soul Flame, and, well, I am an alchemist, so perhaps my qualification should be pushed forward already.
Controlling flames is what I do. And for my age, I know it is embarrassing, but I am 21 years old."

"Wait, are you being serious... 21 years and you have already reached level 3 Core Formation? The last time I checked, only the Pill Princess and the Crystal Prince showed such remarkable talents, each reaching the Core Formation stage at age 50...
So 21 years... this is just..."

"Unbelievable..." Kent smiled. "I know. I could have reached the Core Formation stage faster, but I wasn’t always cultivating, which made some people frustrated. But when I did, which lasted for several days, I managed to reach the Core Formation stage, and they are happy... so it is a win-win for both of us."

The three Half-Elves could only watch Kent with expressions of shock and confusion. They were shocked because, as three nobodies, they had met a genius like Kent... They would tell their generations to come about this moment.
However, they were confused because his words didn’t make sense. At least they couldn’t gather the context of what he said.
But if they knew the brat was talking about his birthday when he had to go dozens of rounds with his wives, perhaps they would have saluted him, giving him the Man of the Year award.

Kent is not the kind of genius they expected. First, he spoke to them freely, with no hint of arrogance around him. Every question asked was accompanied by a smile, one that made them feel like they could relate to him.

That doesn’t scream the arrogant geniuses who look down on the low-born as if they were nothing. He is a genius, one who has proven himself to them, yet he was engaging in conversations and laughing with them.
If this isn’t something worth being proud of, then perhaps the world is not worth living in.

"We don’t know what awaits you, but we will be happy if you join our kind and help us rise above the Elves. I know for sure, you will be able to make a difference for us," Helyra, the emotional one, said with a smile.
"Yeah, well... I had planned on doing that, so let’s hope your king accepts me as part of your race. The rest will handle itself from there."
Kent and the three Half-Elves exited the Flame Valley and started moving toward Elarion.
"By the way, who is the Crystal Prince?" Kent asked as they sped up their movement toward Elarion.
"He is the genius second prince of the Crystal Dragon Race... He joined the Supreme Immortal Sect five years ago and has already become an inner disciple, the last time I heard.

Of course, he isn’t the only genius, but he is popular because he reached the Core Formation stage in 50 years just like the Pill Princess who, from what I know of her, she is both a genius and an arrogant bitch just like her mother."
’Clearly, Helyra has something more against the Elves than his two friends,’ Kent smiled, seeing the disgusted expression on Helyra when she spoke about the Elves...
Whatever it was, he planned on finding out... after all, it isn’t healthy to harbour this much hate within you...

If this isn’t something worth being proud of, then perhaps the world is not worth living in.
"We don’t know what awaits you, but we will be happy if you join our kind and help us rise above the Elves.
I know for sure, you will be able to make a difference for us," Helyra, the emotional one, said with a smile.
"Yeah, well...
I had planned on doing that, so let’s hope your king accepts me as part of your race.
The rest will handle itself from there."
Kent and the three Half-Elves exited the Flame Valley and started moving toward Elarion.
"By the way, who is the Crystal Prince?" Kent asked as they sped up their movement toward Elarion.
"He is the genius second prince of the Crystal Dragon Race...
He joined the Supreme Immortal Sect five years ago and has already become an inner disciple, the last time I heard.

Of course, he isn’t the only genius, but he is popular because he reached the Core Formation stage in 50 years just like the Pill Princess who, from what I know of her, she is both a genius and an arrogant bitch just like her mother."
’Clearly, Helyra has something more against the Elves than his two friends,’ Kent smiled, seeing the disgusted expression on Helyra when she spoke about the Elves...
Whatever it was, he planned on finding out... after all, it isn’t healthy to harbour this much hate within you...

chapters.title: Chapter 709: He Said It [Bonus]
paragraphs: The past week has been a wild one in Elarion; thousands of you geniuses came to register. They all want a chance to prove themselves, and this time, they will have the opportunity.
So, thousands registered, and while thousands were rejected because they didn’t meet the requirements, the others managed to secure a spot in the competition that is set to start in two days.
Registrations are almost over.
Of course, while the Half-Elves thought of it, the other races didn’t send any of their people to come and try to claim a spot from the Half-Elves...

...Well, the other races, such as the Beastkins, Dragons, Dwarves, and the Demons, didn’t send any of their geniuses... except the Elves, who for the past centuries had been trying to suppress the Half-Elves.
While it would be simple for them to do that, the Half-Elves wouldn’t just stand there and let the Elves take everything from them.

They would fight back, and while the ending wouldn’t be ideal for them, they would also succeed in killing most of the Elves... that alone is what is preventing the Elves from going on an all-out war with the Half-Elves.
Naturally, the Half-Elves reproduce faster than the Elves, so number-wise, the Half-Elves have that to spare.

However, while the Elves aren’t declaring war against the Half-Elves, they also aren’t backing down. So, for the past years, they’ve been using one underhanded means after another to try to get the Half-Elves to surrender.

The recent move, which was to deprive them of the 10 slots they had previously allocated to the Half-Elves, was a tactic they had planned to use to lure the Half-Elves in pleading for the five spots they had taken.
And as they say, pleading is the first phase of surrender.

However, the Half-Elves didn’t come or even send a thank-you note back to the Elves like they expected. Instead, the Half Elves made a move that shows the entire world the kind of monsters the Elves are.
They announced an open competition to select five people to represent them when the Flame Tower opens. It was a slap in the face of the Elves.
That was what angered them, prompting them to send five of their best to enter the Half-Elves’ competition and reclaim the five slots they had given them.
At the entrance leading to Elarion, five Elves—four males and a female—stood, glaring at the 35 guards, each standing at the core formation stage, their weapons just within reach.
Yet, they couldn’t gather the courage to make a move against the five Elves.
"Are you preventing us from entering?" Aeric, a green-haired elf wielding a staff, asked, looking smugly at the guards.
The guards gritted their teeth, watching the smug expressions on the faces of the five brats making their lives difficult.

"I thought this was an open competition, which, from the way I see it, just about anyone can participate. I meet all the requirements, and so do my friends, so why are you barring us from entering?" Aeric asked again, but the guards didn’t mind them... they just stood their ground.
They knew that allowing these five to enter meant the chances of their people getting a chance to enter the Flame Tower in three weeks would be virtually nonexistent.
All five are some of the most powerful fire manipulators in the Elven Kingdom...

They are aware of their reputation, and knowing that all five had entered the Flame Tower once and comprehended a Flame Art, the guards knew allowing them to participate would be detrimental to their interests.
The King ordered them not to allow any Elf into the kingdom until the registrations are over.
They can only block them, since attacking will only lead to disaster. If they attack these five, the Elves will find an excuse to retaliate, and that would be too dangerous for them.
So, they were biding their time, and in an hour, they would allow them to enter, which by the time they get there, registrations will be over.
Behind them, some Half-Elves who, due to the blockage, couldn’t enter the city started cursing at the five Elves.
"I never knew shamelessness had a humanoid form until I knew of the Elves. How can they be this shameful to the extent they want to claim the five spots we have?"
"Sometimes, I just want to cut off my ears so people will stop associating me with the Elves. Makes my stomach ick knowing I have their blood flowing through my body."
"Same here. Having a part of them in my lineage makes me want to vomit whenever I meet them."
"That bitch and her people are just too shameful. If I had the means, I would slaughter them all."
As more curses continued to rain down on the prideful Elves, the five started to get irritated.
"All of you, shut up... remember, without us there wouldn’t be you losers." One of the Elves fired back, but the Half-Elves received his insult with a disgusted spat on the ground.
"And what makes you think we want to be associated with you devils? I would rather be a Drow than be called an Elf."
A young man wielding a staff said, glaring at the Elves. He was now coming to register and join the competition, but as it turned out, he would miss the registration.
This made him so angry that he went too far with his insult. But thanks to the heat of the moment, many nodded. However, the Elves didn’t take the insult well.
Aeric, the one who appeared to be the leader of the five, stabbed his staff into the ground, raising three spears made of Earth and Fire.

"Repeat what you said one last time." His words came out cold as the energy around him thickened. Naturally, most started distancing themselves from the Half-Elf who spoke. They could cheer him on, but couldn’t die with him.
The Half-Elf paled when he felt the three flame spears aimed at him...
"I dare you to say it..." Aeric threatened again, but the Half-Elf couldn’t speak. He most definitely didn’t want to die.
"Go ahead, say it."
"He said he would rather become a Drow or perhaps a Dark Elf than be associated with idiots like you..." Suddenly, a voice spoke as a handsome human sauntered and stopped beside the Half-Elf.
"He said it. What are you going to do about it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 710: Tis I, Kent Madson, But You Can Call Me Chaos [Bonus]
paragraphs: The place was already quiet when Aeric prepared to attack the Half-Elf who claimed Drows are better than Elves. It was a grave insult, one that reached deep within the hearts of the five Elves.
So, when Aeric raised the three spears lit on flames, the whole place fell silent. Of course, everyone knew he wouldn’t attack the Half-Elf if he didn’t repeat what he said.
Aeric was merely making a statement..
However, to everyone’s shock, someone boldly spoke the words and even added Dark Elves to the mix, making the whole situation even worse.
Kent walked toward the stunned Half-Elf and placed his hands on his shoulder. A small smile tugged at the corner of his lips as he looked at Aeric...
"He said it. What are you going to do about it?"
Everyone tensed when Kent tempted Aeric. It was a blatant display of pure stupidity in everyone’s point of view... and they were probably right.
But they hadn’t met Kent—not when he was actually looking forward to joining the competition; yet, some people with overprivileged leverage in life stood in his way.
Kent focused his attention on the Elf for a full minute before a sigh escaped his lips. Then he spoke...
"Since you don’t have the spine to attack, then can you pack and leave... some of us actually want to get into the city.

Of course, if you want to join the competition, then perhaps go for a blood transfusion, infuse human blood into your body, and become a Half-Elf. I am sure that will solve your issue. But for now, get out of my way before I make you."
Aeric and his four friends shuddered, hearing what Kent said. Aeric, in particular, trembled with anger as he raised his staff and swung it forward.

The three spears blazed and shot toward Kent, aiming to draw blood from his body. However, before they could even get within a meter of Kent, he waved his hand, and sword arcs sliced through the spears.
Huh.
Their eyes widened when they saw what had happened.
When Aeric attacked, they held their breath, knowing Kent or the Half-Elf was about to die, but that didn’t happen. Kent merely swung his hand, and the spears were neutralized.
"Who are you, and why are you taunting me? Don’t, for one, think I won’t kill you even if it provokes a war between my race and your kind," Aeric said, pointing his staff at Kent.

"Stupid... Do you think I have any reservations about killing you? If you don’t believe me, why don’t you pay attention to my ears?" Kent smirked, noticing how people ignore the ears around this part of the world.
’Was it only me who paid attention to the ear?’ he wondered, looking at the five Elves who now held shocked expressions on their faces, realizing who was messing with them.
The Half-Elves were the same.

The last time they saw a human was several years ago, so they were shocked to see one now. Of course, the humans who came to their kingdom left much faster in fear that the Elves would track them there.
But for a human to be tempting and taunting Elves, this was their first time seeing one. Also, judging by how Kent spoke, he wasn’t showing any sign of fear, meaning he wasn’t leaving anytime soon.
Perhaps if Aeric hated the Half-Elves, then he despised humans, and Kent could see it in his eyes now.
"You are a human."
"Tis I, Kent Madson, but you can call me Chaos." For a moment, the place went quiet until suddenly the five Elves moved and surrounded Kent. The Half-Elf beside Kent tensed.
"You are Kent Madson... We have orders to kill any Kent Madson we see on sight." Aeric raised his staff, causing several spears to float in the air. Each spear was lit on fire.

Aeric turned to the guards. "So the Half-Elves are also colluding with a known fugitive. I will be sure to report this to every race... I am sure they will love to come for an explanation from your useless kind."
"For now, we will handle him... but trust me, you all are doomed."
"What nonsense are you talking about... We’ve never met this human before," one of the guards said, but Aeric turned his attention away from him. His gaze was locked on Kent.
"You can surrender now or die." The dozens of spears burned eerily, waiting to go into battle. All five Elves were ready to take down Kent.

The Half-Elves, especially Arion, Cyran, and Helyra, wore shocked expressions, not knowing what to believe. The Kent they had been with for the past hour had now been branded a fugitive who was ordered to be brought in dead or alive.
That just didn’t make sense. The Kent they knew wasn’t the kind of person they pictured as a fugitive. But as it stood, dozens of spears hovered, ready to attack and take him down.

Kent looked at the five Elves and smirked. "Aren’t you cutting your coat too large? I mean, you may be some big-shot geniuses among the Elves, but in front of me, you are children. I can kill you all in under a second.

That is how insignificant you are. Of course, knowing how foolish some people can be, I will assume your elders didn’t tell you they are working for The Hand because, as far as I am concerned, they were the only ones I offended.
Not that those idiots didn’t deserve that. I will one day kill them all
Of course, you five won’t be leaving here alive today..." Kent paused and spoke again.
"One of you will be leaving here alive today, because you will have to take the bodies of the dead ones back to your Queen." Kent paused again and looked at the Half-Elf beside him.
"Should I kill them?" The young man froze, unsure of what to say, but when asked such a question, he shook his head in response.

"Fine. You all can keep your lives today, but it will take some healing to regrow your limbs." Kent flashed a smile, causing Aeric to attack. However, before the spears could move, Kent acted, drawing his sword.

chapters.title: Chapter 711: Kent Madson [Bonus]
paragraphs: It was an instantaneous movement, one that happened in under a second. But that was all Kent needed to execute his move.
He first appeared before Aeric, and with a quick swing, he took off both hands at shoulder level. Kent didn’t hesitate to go for that precise strike.
He moved and severed one arm and one leg from the second elf, a rather handsome blonde who had chosen to come against him. That didn’t stop Kent from cutting them off.

Both his sword-wielding arm and dominant right leg were taken off before Kent appeared in front of the next one. He was a dark-haired elf, also handsome, like an elf should be. For him, Kent took both legs off and then appeared before the next guy.
Kent showed favoritism by not attacking the lady among them. But who could blame him... The elf lady was rather beautiful to be amputated all of a sudden.
It didn’t sit well with Kent, so he went after the dudes. The lady would take them away for healing. The last one lost both arms just like Aeric.
Kent was back in his original position before many registered what had happened. When they all saw what happened, their eyes widened, fear gripping them.
The screams of the four who had just lost their limbs penetrated everyone’s ears, drawing attention even from within the city.
But Kent wasn’t done. He flicked his arm, and the severed limbs on the ground were burned, to the horror of everyone watching.
When the last limb was burnt to ash, Kent turned to the only remaining elf—the lady.

"You can take them away thanks to this young man saving their lives. Like I said, I would have killed all four of them and burned their bodies, leaving only their heads... But thanks to him, I will let them keep their lives for today."

That said, you should tell your people something for me." Kent smiled. "Tell them I, Kent Madson, said, ’I don’t have a grudge against them, but if they choose to become dogs for the Hand, then I will have no problem cutting them down.’
That will be all, so run along."
The elf lady, fear seeping into her soul, flew into the air, the four lifting off after her. With her impeccable control of spiritual Qi, she was able to carry them effortlessly.
After she was gone from sight, Kent turned to the guards.

"My name is Kent Madson, a human from the Human Continent. I came here by crossing the treacherous Black Sea and traversing the Flame Valley through the Core region. So naturally, I have no plans of turning back now.

And as you all saw, I am an enemy of the Hand and a potential enemy of your kind. Of course, I have no plans to attack any Half-Elves, considering I am here to compete for a chance to enter the Flame Tower.
So let us all get along." He ended his sentence with a smile, causing those who had just witnessed the public display of brutality to swallow nervously.
Kent didn’t bother about their scared expressions. He was looking straight at the city gate. "What do you guys think? Are you opening the door, or should I introduce myself again?"
The guards exchanged uneasy glances, their hands subtly moving toward their weapons, though none dared to make the first move. The tension in the air was thick, like the calm before a storm.

Finally, the tallest among them stepped forward, his voice shaky but firm. "We... we will open the gates. But we will have to escort you in. This is just a precaution in case you feel like pulling out your weapon again."
Kent chuckled, amused by the guard’s words. "You are funny. However, rest assured, I have no plans of pulling out my sword if you don’t pull yours."
"Very well. We will allow your entry."
Kent’s lips curled into a confident smirk. "That’s all I ask."

With a slow, deliberate motion, the guards signaled for the massive iron gates to be unlocked. The guards had already informed their superiors, so allowing Kent in was to ensure he remained within the city’s confines.
They don’t want him running, in case their leaders wish to have him captured. After the gate opened, Kent’s eyes landed on a magnificent city spread into the distance.
However, his attention was immediately drawn to the five guards standing at the entrance to the city gate.
Just a glance was enough to tell Kent they were different from the ones outside
They had this danger in their gaze, one that Kent felt from some of the flame beasts he killed. That look told him quite enough.
Then, if that wasn’t enough, their armor was deep black with reddish runic patterns on it. Per Kent’s knowledge, he knew the runes were for defense.
And, judging by how complex they looked, such runes wouldn’t be found on an ordinary guard’s armor.
"The king ordered the human named Kent Madson to be brought to the palace immediately," one of the new guards shouted, drawing even more attention.
"Oh, come on... At the very least, allow me to explore the city and take in the sights first. I also have to register for the competition," Kent said, sounding like he had been dealt an injustice.
"This is no longer a request. Follow us to the palace on your terms, or we will drag you there."

"Tsk," Kent smirked and then stepped through the gate. But before he left with them, Kent turned and, without saying any names, shouted, "I will look for you guys later." With that, he walked away, causing all those who saw Kent’s brutality to sigh.
"That was intense..."
"Indeed. I felt like I was staring at the Demon King who came down from hell to eat us mortals."
"I mean, aren’t humans considered to be at the bottom of the food chain? If that is true, then how could one of them amputate four powerful Elves just like that?"
The question hung in the air as the wind carried it all over Elarion, reaching almost everyone, even before the end of the day...
