Kent was back in his original position before many registered what had happened.
When they all saw what happened, their eyes widened, fear gripping them.
The screams of the four who had just lost their limbs penetrated everyone’s ears, drawing attention even from within the city.
But Kent wasn’t done.
He flicked his arm, and the severed limbs on the ground were burned, to the horror of everyone watching.
When the last limb was burnt to ash, Kent turned to the only remaining elf—the lady.
"You can take them away thanks to this young man saving their lives.
Like I said, I would have killed all four of them and burned their bodies, leaving only their heads...
But thanks to him, I will let them keep their lives for today."
That said, you should tell your people something for me." Kent smiled.
"Tell them I, Kent Madson, said, ’I don’t have a grudge against them, but if they choose to become dogs for the Hand, then I will have no problem cutting them down.’
That will be all, so run along."
The elf lady, fear seeping into her soul, flew into the air, the four lifting off after her.
With her impeccable control of spiritual Qi, she was able to carry them effortlessly.
After she was gone from sight, Kent turned to the guards.
"My name is Kent Madson, a human from the Human Continent.
I came here by crossing the treacherous Black Sea and traversing the Flame Valley through the Core region.
So naturally, I have no plans of turning back now.
And as you all saw, I am an enemy of the Hand and a potential enemy of your kind.
Of course, I have no plans to attack any Half-Elves, considering I am here to compete for a chance to enter the Flame Tower.
So let us all get along." He ended his sentence with a smile, causing those who had just witnessed the public display of brutality to swallow nervously.
Kent didn’t bother about their scared expressions.
He was looking straight at the city gate.
"What do you guys think?
Are you opening the door, or should I introduce myself again?"
The guards exchanged uneasy glances, their hands subtly moving toward their weapons, though none dared to make the first move.
The tension in the air was thick, like the calm before a storm.
Finally, the tallest among them stepped forward, his voice shaky but firm.
"We... we will open the gates.
But we will have to escort you in.
This is just a precaution in case you feel like pulling out your weapon again."
Kent chuckled, amused by the guard’s words.
"You are funny.
However, rest assured, I have no plans of pulling out my sword if you don’t pull yours."
"Very well.
We will allow your entry."
Kent’s lips curled into a confident smirk.
"That’s all I ask."
With a slow, deliberate motion, the guards signaled for the massive iron gates to be unlocked.
The guards had already informed their superiors, so allowing Kent in was to ensure he remained within the city’s confines.
They don’t want him running, in case their leaders wish to have him captured.
After the gate opened, Kent’s eyes landed on a magnificent city spread into the distance.
However, his attention was immediately drawn to the five guards standing at the entrance to the city gate.
Just a glance was enough to tell Kent they were different from the ones outside
They had this danger in their gaze, one that Kent felt from some of the flame beasts he killed.
That look told him quite enough.
Then, if that wasn’t enough, their armor was deep black with reddish runic patterns on it.
Per Kent’s knowledge, he knew the runes were for defense.
And, judging by how complex they looked, such runes wouldn’t be found on an ordinary guard’s armor.
"The king ordered the human named Kent Madson to be brought to the palace immediately," one of the new guards shouted, drawing even more attention.
"Oh, come on...
At the very least, allow me to explore the city and take in the sights first.
I also have to register for the competition," Kent said, sounding like he had been dealt an injustice.
"This is no longer a request.
Follow us to the palace on your terms, or we will drag you there."
"Tsk," Kent smirked and then stepped through the gate.
But before he left with them, Kent turned and, without saying any names, shouted, "I will look for you guys later." With that, he walked away, causing all those who saw Kent’s brutality to sigh.
"That was intense..."
"Indeed.
I felt like I was staring at the Demon King who came down from hell to eat us mortals."
"I mean, aren’t humans considered to be at the bottom of the food chain?
If that is true, then how could one of them amputate four powerful Elves just like that?"
The question hung in the air as the wind carried it all over Elarion, reaching almost everyone, even before the end of the day...

chapters.title: Chapter 712: Meeting King Thalirion
paragraphs: (Somewhere in Elarion)
"Have you heard? A human is in Elarion right now..." The Bradas Inn is the primary hotspot for the latest gossip in town. If you want something dispersed swiftly, going there is a good idea.
Of course, those who want to hear the latest gossip go there to drink and walk away with the information they came for.
Nobody comes there without a reason. Today, someone brought up another hot topic, and this time, many joined in on the conversation.
"I know, right? I heard he was escorted to the king’s palace by the royal guards as soon as he entered the city."
"I also heard that. But some are saying he severed the limbs of four Elves who came to disturb the competition and made the fifth carry them away."
"That part is true... I was there and saw everything. He is one scary human."
"Are all humans that scary? I don’t think I can sleep tonight after witnessing such a brutal sight."

Words started going around, and while Kent doesn’t know it, his arrival has already reached countless people, causing both panic and intrigue among the Half-Elves. Of course, most of the words going around were exaggerated.
However, one thing was common: everyone is now aware of the presence of a human in Elarion, and that alone is enough to make many start to wonder what this means.

All they heard about this human’s arrival, they wanted to see what it meant for their kind. Is he a good fortune for standing up to the Elves, or a bad seed, one that is too rotten to have among the good seed?
(On the way to the King’s palace)
Kent was fascinated by the grandeur of Elarion. Every building was constructed from the finest woods, showcasing exceptional craftsmanship.

The buildings were elegant, and seeing how perfectly they were aligned, it was clear the formation protecting them had a central hub—somewhere everything was precisely configured and under someone’s control.
Kent was taken aback by the futuristic nature of how they had retrofitted their buildings with formations. It was as if they were prepared for unwanted visitors.
Yes.
While normal eyes couldn’t see it, Kent could perceive that every single building was part of an attacking formation—one that could easily kill a Core Formation expert if they became careless.
’These people are careful,’ Kent thought inwardly, studying the complex formations woven into each building.

’They have everything perfectly set up, and while I don’t have to fear soul attacks, the amount of soul energy gathered in this formation could even injure a Spirit Ascension stage cultivator.’ Kent nodded, moving in the middle of five people.
Two were on his right, two on his left, and their captain was in the front.
Kent studied their presence for a few seconds and then sighed. ’They are not readable even by my Enchanted eyes.’
Kent wanted to see their aura to figure out what to do or how to approach the conversation when he got to the king. But no matter how hard he tried, he couldn’t.
It seems some serious enchantment protects the guards...perhaps a formation.
’I guess I should be prepared for anything,’ Kent said to himself.
A few minutes later, they arrived in front of an elegant gate guarded by two guards clad in the same armor as those who had come to pick him up.
The door opened, and Kent stepped into a large compound featuring many buildings. Just like the buildings outside, these were also made from the finest wood and adorned with intricate formations.
Kent didn’t have the luxury to explore the entire place, but he knew that all the formations in the city were linked to this mansion, where the king lived.
’This place is rather interesting. Looks like I will have more fun here than I expected.’ Along the way, Kent sensed someone’s gaze on him.
It wasn’t intense or hostile, but as someone who had broken limits on his cultivation, mind, and soul, the slightest change in someone’s presence was enough to capture his attention.
Kent turned to look at who was staring at him. However, the person was quick to move away and disappear from his sight. Still, he caught the shadow of the person and knew it was a lady.
Though Kent wasn’t sure if his eyes were deceiving him, since there was no killing intent behind the gaze he felt, he knew it was all good.
After moving for a couple of minutes, they came to a stop in front of a building. From the outside, it appeared to be a rectangular-shaped structure, but Kent knew that wasn’t the case.
The building was actually a perfect square.
However, the formation made it appear rectangular. He had no idea why, but he had a few theories to explain it.
Kent circled the building in his mind, analyzing every detail he could perceive. The formation’s subtle distortion wasn’t just for aesthetics; it served a deeper purpose.

’Perhaps it’s designed to confuse hostile intruders or disrupt enemy formation readings,’ Kent mused. ’Or maybe it’s a strategic defense to mask the true layout from aerial or soul-based reconnaissance.’
His theory may ultimately prove unfounded, but Kent knew that the altered shape of the building held a deeper meaning.
’Nobody in their right mind would spend countless hours weaving formations just to change the shape of a building. It must serve a greater function...’
Kent followed the guards as they entered the hall. It was spacious inside as well.
Yet, while that was obvious, Kent’s attention was drawn to the figures within. The slender man with short brown hair seated on the throne was King Thalirion, whom Kent already knew from his scan.
Besides him, there were ten others, each radiating the peak of the Core Formation stage power. Their auras had been refined so precisely that it seemed almost nonexistent.
But that was what made them dangerous—such mastery over their aura meant they had exceptional control over spiritual energy. That made them formidable.
’This place keeps getting more impressive the more I see,’ Kent thought inwardly, stepping forward toward the king and his lords.
"My King, this is Kent Madson..." the leader of the guards announced the moment they approached the throne.

chapters.title: Chapter 713: Nonchalant Kent
paragraphs: The ten Elders in the hall and the King were visibly shaken when they saw Kent. It wasn’t because Kent was too handsome to the point that they couldn’t fathom his good looks...
Their shock stemmed from the fact that, among the many rumors circulating about Kent Madson, the person in question was merely a level three Core Formation Expert.
Until today, they had expected Kent to be some big shot, someone with power so great that killing him would require the assistance of an entire race.
They expected Kent to look so scary that just laying eyes on him would be enough to make you pee your pants. They expected Kent to be the most dangerous person they had ever met...
But looking at him now, they just couldn’t bring themselves to pee their pants or run away screaming.
Kent was just normal, and aside from his handsomeness, they didn’t feel any threat from him.

King Thalirion looked at Kent curiously for a few seconds and then spoke, "You are Kent Madson?" It was a question containing many skeptical remarks, one aimed at knowing just what the fuck was going on.
Was the Hand messing with them by claiming Kent was dangerous? Or was he really that strong but appeared harmless to deceive everyone? Nothing made sense to the king and his Elders...
Kent looked at everyone and nodded. "I am Kent Madson... Nice meeting you all."
The Elders looked at Kent, scanning him from head to toe. Of course, the fact that Kent didn’t seem agitated or scared told them how he felt.
’He isn’t afraid of us... Almost like we aren’t much of a threat to him... But that just doesn’t make sense.’
The King and his Elders thought the same thing.
"May I know why you are here?" the king asked. For someone being hunted by the Hand, though he appeared harmless, it was better to tread carefully.
"I am here to join the competition to gain access to the Flame Tower... Though my end game is to get into the Supreme Immortal Sect."
"You are not a Half-Elf," the King said.
"I know. However, a little bird told me that this is an open competition, so I can compete if I meet the requirements... As it turns out, I meet all the requirements." Kent smiled.
The Elders looked at the king and then back at Kent.
"Registrations are over... So I am sorry, but you may have come here for nothing," the King said, keeping a straight face.
Kent studied his expression for a few moments before a sigh escaped his lips.
"I understand. In that case, I will leave then..." Kent looked at the King and his elders for a few more seconds.
"Whatever the Hand is offering you, don’t even consider it. Trust me, going against me is the last thing you want to do... But you can call them and tell them where I am..."
Kent turned and started walking away from the hall under the shocked gaze of the King and his elders. They just didn’t understand what had happened.

It was true that registrations were over, but this was the king; he had the means to add one more candidate to the list of registered candidates. However, instead of Kent pleading with him to do so, he turned to leave.
But if that wasn’t shocking enough, he even told them to call the people after him and give them his location. It was like he didn’t care about his life, so he wanted it to end.
But the most shocking part was the subtle threat he left them, as if he was making sure they understood he wasn’t afraid of them, not even in the slightest.
"Wait," King Thalirion said, halting Kent in his tracks. He turned and looked back at the King.
"Are you just going to leave like that? Aren’t you even going to try to get a spot in the competition? I know you came a long way for this. Aren’t the Flame Tower what you are after?"
Kent smiled slightly. "I indeed came a long way for this. However, since I couldn’t get a chance to see her, I planned to try my luck somewhere else.

I came here because I was told the Half-Elves are more welcoming to humans than the other races. But since I won’t be getting a chance here, I might as well try my luck somewhere else. I am sure I will get a slot one way or the other."
The King turned and looked at his elders as if they should say something. He hadn’t expected the conversation to go in this direction.
He expected Kent to be more desperate. He expected him to beg for a chance to compete for a slot to enter the Flame Tower.
This way, if things had gone like he expected, he would have some leverage to know more about why Kent was being hunted down by the Hand.
However, as if he weren’t even interested in what he had come there for, Kent just turned to leave. This broke the expectations he had of Kent...

The King and his elders were taken aback, unsure of what to say. They had never met someone who could show such a degree of nonchalance when something as precious as entering the Flame Tower was on the line.
"You all might want to take my offer and contact the Hand, or else the Elves will beat you to it. Although I must say, I am a little disappointed that my expectations for coming here weren’t met.
But I understand. This isn’t something I can force, regardless of how much I need this. I came here peacefully; I will leave the same way I came."
"What if we give you a spot to compete? Would that be enough to tell us why the Hand is after you?" The King, ever the conscientious man, still wanted to know more about Kent.

He wasn’t about to make a mistake by calling the Hand when he didn’t know everything. Something told him turning Kent in would be bad for them, so he wanted to know, and if the ending were bad, he would handle that one too.

chapters.title: Chapter 714: The Rich Young Master [Bonus]
paragraphs: Inwardly, Kent was laughing at the King.
’I guess all those acting classes Mama made me take weren’t wasted.’ He smiled and then focused his attention on the King.
"Are you sure you want to know why I am being hunted by the Hand?" Kent asked, and the King nodded.
"Very well. But this may come as a shock to you because I don’t even know why they want me dead, though I have some theories.
First, through one of their informants, I managed to send them a catchy notice that I am aware of their existence. That pissed them off, so they came after me... bringing me to the second theory.
I killed thousands of their men, rendering their plans to send a message to everyone that they are not to be messed with, obsequious. That was a massive blow to them.
Then they sent the one called ’the Hunter,’ who, as it turns out, wasn’t so bad. One led to another, and we are now buddies."
"Wait, did you just say the Hunter came after you?" Lord Faelen cut Kent off before he could end his theories.
Kent looked at him and then smiled. "But of course. She isn’t too bad if you get to know her." The elders looked at each other and then at their king.
"And as I was saying, after the Hunter failed, I had to send them a new message, and this time, I made them aware of the consequences if they were unable to meet my expectations.

I mean, for such an organization claiming to be the best in the world, they sure don’t behave like one. So I gave them a notice that they shouldn’t mess with me, and judging by how the Elves reacted at the gate, the Hand is serious about ending me now."
Kent smiled weakly. "Poor souls, they will be dying for nothing."
"You make it sound like you can handle them," King Thalirion said ever so sneakily, making Kent, who understood what he was doing, laugh.
"Let’s just say if I put my mind to it, killing everyone in the world wouldn’t be as hard as you might think."
Quiet.

The King and his elders fell silent upon hearing Kent’s words. It sounded ridiculous, but to them, knowing that the most dangerous underworld organization was hunting Kent, they sensed the danger in his words.
This made them wonder just what Kent was trying to say. However, Kent didn’t allow them to think that far.

"Look, I am not afraid of the Hand. If they don’t understand that yet, they will soon come to understand. Because trust me, I am not as simple as I appear. So you choose: become my enemy now, or become friends, which is a huge gamble—but know all too well that becoming my friend will end well for you and your people."
Kent smiled. "Now, how about the competition? Giving me a chance means you will be sending one of your own to the sect this year.
But aside from that, I can help the other four enter the sect, provided I get to be one of the five to enter the Flame Tower.
Of course, I am not asking to be given special treatment, but a chance to compete for a slot is all I ask for..."
Kent waved his hand, and eleven grapes appeared. Waving his hand again, the grapes flew and landed in the palms of the elders and the king.
"You can enjoy some grapes while you determine what road to take." The smile on Kent’s face was that of a world-class scammer who knew he had set his bait in the heads of the elders and the king.
And adding the 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruit was something the King and his people wouldn’t even know how to process.
Looking at their shocked expressions, Kent smiled slightly.
It was a bribe, but one they couldn’t reject.

Kent took a handful of the grapes and started eating. This sight scared the King and his people. The last time they saw a Spirit Grape Fruit was at an auction held at the Qilin Garden, somewhere in the Beast Empire.
It sold for billions of spirit stones. So they knew how expensive a Spirit Grape Fruit was. But watching Kent eat them like normal fruit, they just couldn’t wrap their minds around it.
"No need to look so shocked, everyone. It is just a 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruit..."
"WHAT?"
The king couldn’t keep his composure anymore. His hands were shaking as he held the grape. The last Spirit Grape Fruit they saw was 500 years old, but even that was sold for billions.
However, in their hands now was a 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruit. What did this mean...
’Just one of these has the means to raise the standard of living for my people,’ the king thought, looking as Kent threw one grape after another into his mouth, smiling at him.
’Who is this human?’ the king wondered.

"Fine. I know I was stingy for giving you each just one grape. So, how about this? Add me to the competition, and then afterward, I will provide you with 1,000 more of these and even help the four Half-Elves that will be entering the Flame Tower raise their spirit roots to the Immortal grade.
How does that sound?"
The King’s mouth was wide open.
Sitting at the core of the universe, Lady Universe smiled, which gradually turned into a resounding laughter.
"You know, due to how chaotic he is, I sometimes forget he is also shameless and a good scammer," the Enchantress’ voice entered Lady Universe’s ears.
"What do you expect? Someone who managed to scam me before is no normal person."
"That was funny. I remember how you were so pissed and wanted to kill him. I wonder what would have happened if you truly killed him back then."
"Ha," Lady Universe chuckled, "I guess we wouldn’t know now, do we?"
"I guess so, too. But isn’t the fact that he is everything a person would want to be the point we both have become creeps watching his every moment?"
Both the Enchantress and Lady Universe blushed.
"Mortals are just funny... Look at their funny expressions."

sentences.text: Inwardly, Kent was laughing at the King.
’I guess all those acting classes Mama made me take weren’t wasted.’ He smiled and then focused his attention on the King.
"Are you sure you want to know why I am being hunted by the Hand?" Kent asked, and the King nodded.
"Very well.
But this may come as a shock to you because I don’t even know why they want me dead, though I have some theories.
First, through one of their informants, I managed to send them a catchy notice that I am aware of their existence.
That pissed them off, so they came after me... bringing me to the second theory.
I killed thousands of their men, rendering their plans to send a message to everyone that they are not to be messed with, obsequious.
That was a massive blow to them.
Then they sent the one called ’the Hunter,’ who, as it turns out, wasn’t so bad.
One led to another, and we are now buddies."
"Wait, did you just say the Hunter came after you?" Lord Faelen cut Kent off before he could end his theories.
Kent looked at him and then smiled.
"But of course.
She isn’t too bad if you get to know her." The elders looked at each other and then at their king.
"And as I was saying, after the Hunter failed, I had to send them a new message, and this time, I made them aware of the consequences if they were unable to meet my expectations.
I mean, for such an organization claiming to be the best in the world, they sure don’t behave like one.
So I gave them a notice that they shouldn’t mess with me, and judging by how the Elves reacted at the gate, the Hand is serious about ending me now."
Kent smiled weakly.
"Poor souls, they will be dying for nothing."
"You make it sound like you can handle them," King Thalirion said ever so sneakily, making Kent, who understood what he was doing, laugh.
"Let’s just say if I put my mind to it, killing everyone in the world wouldn’t be as hard as you might think."
Quiet.
The King and his elders fell silent upon hearing Kent’s words.
It sounded ridiculous, but to them, knowing that the most dangerous underworld organization was hunting Kent, they sensed the danger in his words.
This made them wonder just what Kent was trying to say.
However, Kent didn’t allow them to think that far.
"Look, I am not afraid of the Hand.
If they don’t understand that yet, they will soon come to understand.
Because trust me, I am not as simple as I appear.
So you choose: become my enemy now, or become friends, which is a huge gamble—but know all too well that becoming my friend will end well for you and your people."
Kent smiled.
"Now, how about the competition?
Giving me a chance means you will be sending one of your own to the sect this year.
But aside from that, I can help the other four enter the sect, provided I get to be one of the five to enter the Flame Tower.
Of course, I am not asking to be given special treatment, but a chance to compete for a slot is all I ask for..."

This sight scared the King and his people.

So they knew how expensive a Spirit Grape Fruit was.
But watching Kent eat them like normal fruit, they just couldn’t wrap their minds around it.
"No need to look so shocked, everyone.
It is just a 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruit..."
"WHAT?"
The king couldn’t keep his composure anymore.
His hands were shaking as he held the grape.
The last Spirit Grape Fruit they saw was 500 years old, but even that was sold for billions.
However, in their hands now was a 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruit.
What did this mean...
’Just one of these has the means to raise the standard of living for my people,’ the king thought, looking as Kent threw one grape after another into his mouth, smiling at him.
’Who is this human?’ the king wondered.
"Fine.
I know I was stingy for giving you each just one grape.
So, how about this?

Add me to the competition, and then afterward, I will provide you with 1,000 more of these and even help the four Half-Elves that will be entering the Flame Tower raise their spirit roots to the Immortal grade.
How does that sound?"
The King’s mouth was wide open.
Sitting at the core of the universe, Lady Universe smiled, which gradually turned into a resounding laughter.
"You know, due to how chaotic he is, I sometimes forget he is also shameless and a good scammer," the Enchantress’ voice entered Lady Universe’s ears.
"What do you expect?
Someone who managed to scam me before is no normal person."
"That was funny.
I remember how you were so pissed and wanted to kill him.
I wonder what would have happened if you truly killed him back then."
"Ha," Lady Universe chuckled, "I guess we wouldn’t know now, do we?"
"I guess so, too.
But isn’t the fact that he is everything a person would want to be the point we both have become creeps watching his every moment?"
Both the Enchantress and Lady Universe blushed.
"Mortals are just funny...
Look at their funny expressions."

chapters.title: Chapter 715: Kent Madson Has Appeared [Bonus]
paragraphs: (Elven Kingdom: Sylveria - The Queen’s Palace)
*BANG!*
The Elf Queen slammed the arm of her throne, creating cracks in it.
"What did you just say..." she asked in a stern tone, one that prevented Brilanna, the Elf lady, whom Kent had let go after severing the arms of the four from speaking immediately.
Eventually, she repeated what she said.
"Kent Madson is Elarion... my Queen," Brilanna repeated her words, causing the Elf Queen and the five elders with her to clench their fists.

"What should we do, My Queen?" Lord Arlen asked in a furious tone. They might have relaxed a bit when such news reached them, but hearing that four of their best were amputated and that Kent had even sent a warning message made them very angry.
They wanted nothing more now than to sever the arms on Kent’s body and boil his flesh in boiling oil, all while seasoning him with the hottest pepper in the world.
"Send men to Elarion. Tell them to hand over Kent Madson. If they refuse, report to me immediately," the queen said before vanishing from the throne room.
(Elwood Gardens - somewhere in Sylveria)
Lady Aelith, the ancestor of the Elves and once a formidable warrior who participated in the Battle of Parting 25,000 years ago, sat in a serene garden, watching birds.
She was just a Root Master back then, but she fought alongside Root Grandmasters and Root Saints, killing many while coming close to death’s door a few times.
After the battle, when the queen ascended, she stepped in and led her people for 15,000 years, bringing them to the pinnacle of the world.
However, for the past 10,000 years, she had been in seclusion, strengthening her foundation and doing her best to maximize her strength before ascending.
She had made considerable headway since then.
Now, she came out to have a few years of rest before returning to seclusion. She planned to break two limits before ascending. She had also made progress on that front, already breaking one limit.
However, while she may appear harmless to many, she is one of the most dangerous individuals in the world, posing a threat even to someone like Kent, who has already broken four limits.

When it comes to battle experience, she has more than Kent. She had fought in many battles, killed anyone who stood in her way, and came close to dying several times, so her years of battle experience would trump someone like Kent.
And as it stood, she was Kent’s enemy, only waiting for him to surface so she could handle him. Of course, she wasn’t doing this because the Hand wanted Kent dead; she was after something else.

Learning that Kent was in possession of someone having the Divine Atomic Body, she wanted it. And it wasn’t to raise someone destined to become an excellent assassin in the future, like most would do...
No...
It was for herself. Body constitutions can be stolen just like spirit roots can be stolen. She wanted Li Hua’s heavenly constitution, and she was ready to kill to get it.
Suddenly, Queen Elenara appeared in the garden.
"What is it, Ele?" Lady Aelith asked when her daughter appeared.
"Kent Madson has surfaced."
"Where?"
"Elarion... It appears he is there to take part in the competition organized by the Half-Breeds."
Lady Aelith stood up and walked toward a particular tree, plucking a green-colored fruit. "Don’t contact the Hand yet... I will go there first."
"Okay, mother," Queen Elenara nodded and then left.
"Kent Madson, huh? I wonder what you look like and what you think you will gain coming here." An evil smirk tugged at her lips as she walked away.
(Gray Mountain - Hideout of the Hand)
For an organization whose name is known even to the most common people, they sure know how to conceal their identity.
The Gray Mountain, one of the most dangerous places in the Elven lands, happens to be one of the many hideouts of the Hand.

It is located several miles away from the Flame Valley. However, with the Elves and demons sharing a border, the Gray Mountain is located right at the center, acting as a boundary that separates the two races.

The Hand prefers to act swiftly, so they are situated there and carry out their plans. In the past few weeks, they had sent more men to such hideouts and had been lying in wait for one person to make an appearance.
Of course, that person was Kent Madson. From the Human continent, through the Ancient Battlefield of Parting, and the other continent, their forces have been on alert.
So when the word reached them that Kent Madson had appeared in Elarion, they started gearing up.

"Remember, under no circumstances should any of you back down. Kill him if you can, but if he is as weak as he should be, then capture him. I will be around, so rest assured, he is as good as dead or captured."
"As your command, Lord Tiger Fang."
One of the Seven Fangs of the Hand instructed, his hand crossed behind him. He wore a tiger mask, and judging by his aura, he was no easy warrior.
Soon, hundreds of warriors moved out. Most were experts in the Sovereign stage, but a few had progressed to the Core Formation stage.
After they left, Tiger Fang took a communication crystal and channeled his energy into it.
(The Hand Headquarters)
The Hand, dressed in white with her white hair flowing down her back, sat in a chair reading a scroll. Judging by her expression, she was both intrigued and a little afraid of something.
After a while, a smile appeared on her face.
"Finally, I can cultivate my realm again," she muttered, looking at the contents of the scroll.
"Qilin, wait for me. Thanks to you, I now have a much stronger foundation than ever. After I refine my core to the 7th stage, I will come and take your head off.
The years of humiliation you put me through will end with your head on the ground." For someone draped in white and looking like an angel, her words were rather nasty.
"But first, Kent Madson, I will skin that brat alive. Who does he think he is?"
Suddenly, her communication crystal buzzed. She took it and channeled her energy into it.
"Speak."
"Kent Madson has appeared in Elarion... we are on our way to retrieve him," Tiger Fang said on the other end of the line.
"Keep me updated." The Hand cut the line and walked away.

chapters.title: Chapter 716: Like A Guardian Angel
paragraphs: (Elarion - The King’s Palace)
The revelation Kent made threw the king and his elders into a state of contemplation, leaving them wondering if turning Kent over to the Hand was a wise move or not.
Of course, they didn’t want to become enemies of the Hand—that was the last thing they wanted. So they were drawn into a state of uncertainty.
Then there was the fact that Kent had just offered them an offer they couldn’t refuse. The Spirit Grape Fruit he gave them was enough to raise their soul strength to a new level.
This meant that when offered to the people who would be entering the Flame Tower, their chances of comprehending a Flame Art were high. Flame cultivation mostly relies on the soul.
Of course, Kent said he would be giving them a thousand Spirit Grape Fruits and even help raise the Spirit Root of all four who would be entering the Flame Tower to the Immortal Grade.
That was just too much for them... but to Kent, it was nothing.
So they were caught in a bind, unsure of what to do.
But then Kent told them to contact the Hand and inform them he was in their kingdom. This gave them a way out...one they needed. However...
That was enough to tell them he had no intention of backing out, regardless of what they did. Kent already planned on setting the Hand straight, so he was waiting for them.
At that moment, the King had just informed the Hand of his whereabouts and put down the communication crystal.
"It is done," King Thalirion said with a sigh, unsure if he had just made the biggest mistake of his life. He never expected Kent to be this bold.
"No need to look down, King Thalirion. I am merely making sure that after today, the Hand won’t set their sights on your people. Informing them is the right thing to do.
Now, as promised, here are the 1,000 fruits." Kent produced a pouch containing the fruit, which flew into the king’s waiting arms. Then he retrieved another one.
"Inside this pouch are four Immortal Grade Ambrosia apples. You already know what they can do..." He gave that to the king and started walking away.
"I will be staying with a few friends after I take care of the idiots on the way. And don’t worry, I will ensure no harm comes to your people."
After saying that, Kent walked away. He first headed to the city gate, where he planned to wait for his visitors.
Meanwhile, back at the palace, the king held the two pouches with delicate hands.
"What just happened?" one of the elders asked.
"Did we just receive not one but a thousand 10,000-year-old Spirit Grape Fruits?"
"Not just that, but four Immortal Grade Ambrosia apples. This is just too much by all standards."
The elders were shocked beyond their understanding.
"Is this the reason the Hand wants him dead? To steal his wealth," one of the elders wondered, and the rest couldn’t help but think the same thing.
From their perspective, anyone would want to have a fraction of what Kent has, so it didn’t take much to suspect the Hand wants his wealth.
"I mean, they did say he is wealthy, so I think they want his wealth."
"I think we will be able to raise more geniuses who, in a few years, will bloom into powerful warriors capable of standing toe to toe with the best in the world.
The time for our race to rise has come."
The elders were over the moon.

Even the king couldn’t hold back his smile. "With this, we can finally show the Elves what it means to be hybrids... They have suppressed us for a long time. Finally, we can rise to the peak and challenge them on equal footing."
The elders clenched their fists, feeling anticipation wash through their bodies.
"What about Kent Madson... Do you think he will be fine? Shouldn’t we go help him?" Naturally, as their benefactor, the elders started to worry about him.
However, the king shook his head.
"He said he will handle it, so the least we can do is trust him. If we were to join him, the Hand would start targeting us, and while we may be safe here, our people on the outside wouldn’t be safe.
So we should trust him and see if he can handle it on his own, as he claimed."
The elders nodded, though they still felt like they were betraying Kent.

"Lord Yael, you will be overseeing the competition, so ensure Kent’s name is added to the candidates’ list. Though we don’t know if he qualifies without doing the testing, he did say he met all three requirements."
Lord Yael, a pale-skinned, black-eyed, short-wavy, gray-haired, handsome man in his late 40s, nodded with a smile.
"Lord Zaltarish, be sure to find out who his friends are and make sure their status is raised. They may have just brought us a Guardian Angel."
Lord Zaltarish also nodded with a smile. As someone with Elven heritage, he was undoubtedly handsome, with amber eyes and wild crimson hair.
The elders and the king decided to raise the standard of living for their people immediately. They wanted to ensure they reaped every benefit from the wealth they’d just accumulated.

They no longer had to fear spending their reserve funds; they could tap into their backup funds and other resources. Just one Spirit Grape Fruit was already enough to keep them afloat for years to come.
And now they had 1,000 of those. So, as a race suppressed by others, this was their chance to spread their wings and ensure everyone had something to eat and a place to lay their head.
It wouldn’t be an overnight change, but as it stood, they had gathered enough wealth to make life much more comfortable for everyone.
"Looks like they are here." After about 20 minutes, the king spoke, turning toward the city entrance.
"Let’s go." Though they wouldn’t be joining the battle, they would at least watch. However, regardless of the outcome, they would remain mere observers.

chapters.title: Chapter 717: Mind Mess
paragraphs: At the city entrance, now devoid of people since the gate had long been open and everyone had entered, Kent stood with his arms crossed over his chest, looking down the road that trailed far into the distance.
The guards stood in front of the gate, watching the human who had been standing there for the past five minutes.
"You don’t think the king threw him out... after all, he was escorted in and taken to the king’s palace," one of the guards asked, watching Kent’s back.
"I don’t think he was thrown out. I mean, if the king wanted him out, wouldn’t the royal guards escort him?"
"That makes sense. But then, if the king didn’t throw him out, why is he standing there like a beggar?"
The guards speculated about many things as the watch held back. They didn’t understand why someone who had just antagonized the Elves would be standing outside as if he were waiting for his death.
"CLOSE THE DOORS AND SOUND THE ALARMS!"

Suddenly, the leader of the guards shouted, prompting the gossiping ones to turn to him. When they looked where his gaze was directed, they saw hundreds of Elven warriors, each at the Core Formation stage, flying at top speed toward them.
They immediately scattered, running toward the gate. However, before they could get far, Kent’s voice stopped them.
"They are here for me."

They paused for a second before continuing to run. They didn’t trust Kent, and since they were trained to respond immediately, they closed the door. But before the alarms could sound, the king’s voice entered their ears.
"Don’t sound the alarm. They are here for the human."
The king and the ten elders appeared in the air, stopping atop the gate that overlooked the vast expanse of green land stretching before them.
A few seconds later, the Elves reached the gate, stopping 150 meters away. But as cultivators, such a distance can be closed in microseconds.
One hundred twenty of them hovered in the air, looking coldly at Kent, while one landed on the ground and walked forward, maintaining a distance of 20 meters between him and Kent.
"You are Kent Madson," Dailon, one of the Elf army generals, asked, holding his sword.
Kent looked at him calmly, and then a smile appeared on his face. "You look young and handsome for someone who is already 1,209 years old. Tell me, what is your skincare routine?"
It wasn’t just the Elves; even King Thalirion and the ten elders didn’t expect such a reply from Kent. His answer wasn’t what they expected, given the conditions he found himself in.
However, Kent stood there, looking smugly at General Dailon, who was having a hard time coming to terms with a few things.
Aside from the obviously shocking reply he had received, one thing struck his nerves, causing him to wonder many things. Instinctively, his back broke out in a cold sweat.
’How did he know my age...’ he wondered, looking at Kent.
"No need to look at me like that. I am Kent Madson, so of course, I know every small thing about all of you. For example, you over there," Kent pointed at another Elf hovering among the 120 Elves.

"Your name is Queren, you are 980 years old, and while I hate doing this, sleeping with General Dailon’s wife is not cool. You can’t be doing that to your general while he was away protecting your borders."

"Or you think asking for leave under the pretense that your sister is sick wouldn’t catch someone’s eye. I am disappointed in you, Queren. The Bro Code states that another bro shouldn’t covet another bro’s wife... That is cold of you, Queren... I am disappointed."
Kent turned back to Dailon and sighed, shaking his head in sympathy. "I am sorry you have to find out like this, but that bitch has been banging this traitor for 26 years now.
The only reason she hasn’t become pregnant yet is that this bastard has reasonable control over his release. Cerise loves him for that. I mean, that lying bitch...
You should probably find yourself a new wife when you get back... because I can’t bring myself to kill a fellow brother who was cuckolded.
But don’t worry, as a bro, I will share in your sympathy, so I will leave him for you to handle later, after I kill everyone, of course. Some revenges must be exacted in person."
The look on everyone’s face was one of shock, disbelief, and, even more importantly, bewilderment. No one could understand why Kent knew all he had just said.
It was both terrifying, considering the names he mentioned were all true. The part about Queren asking for leave was true. Dailon could still remember that day vividly.
He even sent his regards to Queren’s sister... Now it turns out he was sending regards to his moaning wife, who chose to bang a dude under his command.
Dailon’s grip tightened on his sword as he recalled the memory. Then there was the part where Kent spoke about Queren having good control of his release, making it impossible to impregnate his wife.
That hit even worse. He felt betrayed, and looking at the calm expression on Kent’s face now, he could tell he was being manipulated, but he couldn’t bring himself to do anything about it.
Kent had gotten inside his head.
Of course, Kent was smiling inwardly. ’That skill I received after adding Elaine to the harem is a gold mine,’ Kent thought.
The skill he received is called [Mind Mess].
It allows him to create confusion among allies. All he has to do is find the weak link and start weaving confusion from there. It’s a slow way of poisoning the mind.

But Kent has something that can speed up the process—his ’Enchanted Eyes.’ They allow him to gain access to the most secret information about someone, depending on how powerful they are and Kent’s own mental and soul strength.
Naturally, Kent saw all 121 Elves before him like an open book. So, using the skill, he targeted the leader... but it was just the start.
"Edyrm, why did you choose to betray your kind, colluding with the Dark Elves to kill Fenris’ parents? Do you hate your best friend that much?"

chapters.title: Chapter 718: Aura of Blood and Chaos [Bonus]
paragraphs: The current happenings at the main entrance of Elarion were something that couldn’t be described with words.
Kent didn’t raise a finger to kill; he merely stood there, speaking...
He was spilling secrets that were never meant to be revealed.
He first started with Dailon, planting the seed of doubt and anger in him. Then, using the [Mind Mess] skill, he made sure Dailon walked the path he had laid out for him.

But he wasn’t the only one targeted. He targeted a few more, and when he was fully at the point where a snap of his finger could send the Elves into a frenzy, clashing with each other, Kent merely smiled and turned to his left.
His main targets had arrived, but the damage he intended had already been dealt. He had forever sown the seed of mistrust in the hearts of 121 Core formation experts.
Beings so powerful that no king would want to lose even one of them.
He made sure that in the next battle they got into, that sense of camaraderie would no longer be with them. They would become strangers, with hate in their hearts as they faced their enemies.
Instead of fighting with their minds and souls, they would go into battle not knowing whether they would feel the sharp sting of the blade of their former friends pierce through their backs.
King Thalirion and his Elders felt a chill run down their spines as they looked at the assembly of 121 warriors broken.
"Is that even possible, to bring an entire team of seasoned warriors to their knees just through words? This is just too much."
"It all happened in under two minutes. Does this mean he only needed that long to dismantle a whole team of able fighters?"
"Just who is this human?"
Kent wasn’t thinking about any of that since his main target had arrived. Surprisingly, right when the Hand warriors arrived, Lady Aelith also appeared, much faster than the Hand.
Kent was taken aback by her sudden presence, and judging by the shift in the air, she wasn’t like the weak Elves he toyed with.
Lady Aelith walked calmly in the air, passing by the 120 Elves still suspended in the air. "Trash," her words were laced with disdain and fury.
She walked by them and then gazed down at Kent. She moved one step and was 10 meters away from Kent. However, before she could say anything, King Thalirion spoke, stepping forward.
"Ancestor Aelith, what brings you here?" His words contained just enough touch of warning, one that Kent read the moment the King called the new arrival an Ancestor.
Of course, Kent knew quite a lot about her since he had already scanned her. ’She is dangerous... but still lacking.’
Lady Aelith looked at King Thalirion for a second before she ignored him. To her, talking to King Thalirion was like swimming in mud with pigs. That is how much she hated the Half-Elves.
"You are Kent Madson," Lady Aelith said, looking coldly at Kent. It was apparent she didn’t come there to know his name since she was already oozing killing intent.
Kent maintained his calm expression, but inwardly, he was grinning. ’This is a perfect time to test the other skill, which also has something to do with the mind.’

"I don’t suppose we met before, young lady. I am Kent Madson, but you can call me Big Daddy Kent. Of course, if it is too early, you can call me Grandpa Kent..." Kent flashed her a smile, "What do you say?"
There was already silence when Kent spoke, but now it was as if all sounds in the world were sucked out. Even breathing was something no one around was doing. Kent’s bold words left them speechless.
But it got worse.

’Did he call the ancestor of the Elves "young lady"... is he not afraid of death? That is Lady Aelith, damnit. Even we, Half-Elves, had to respect someone like her, despite our issues with the long ears.
But this young man disrespected her, and looking at her, she would probably explode any moment and break every bone in his body.’ King Thalirion feared for Kent’s life.
As expected, before he even ended his words, a thick, suffocating aura burst out of her body, surrounding Kent immediately.
King Thalirion and his Elders moved back, so did the guards and the 121 Elven warriors. The Hand warriors who appeared even stepped back, not willing to be in the blast radius.

However, no blast came. Because the moment the aura landed on Kent’s body, a smile appeared on his face. ’Thick aura, filled with her years of killing. But she is nowhere near Chaos... and I am Chaos.’

Kent looked at the lady and smirked, "I didn’t come from the Human Continent, travel across the black Sea for you, lady, so step aside. My beef is with them." Kent waved his hand, and the aura Lady Aelith spent 25,000 years refining was brushed aside just like that.

Her body trembled—not from anger, but from unrestrained fear, one she only felt during the Battle of Parting. Back then, she was a Root master who managed to kill loads of Root Grandmasters and a few Root Saints.

However, during the battle, she was nearly killed by a Root Transcendent. Back then, she was terrified beyond her wits. But when she survived, she promised herself she would never feel that way again, and she kept that promise for 25,000 years.
However, just like 25,000 years ago, a mere human—someone who is not even one-eighth of her power—brushed aside her aura and looked at her like she were a greenhouse flower.
It was like Kent didn’t even feel anything.

Naturally, Kent didn’t feel anything, as his own aura had changed so much that he never even noticed. It turns out that entering the Realm of Blood and Chaos had a much greater effect on his aura, one filled with the primal fury born out of blood and carnage.
And now that Kent had discovered this, he felt the need to taste blood. So he turned to the Hand, and an evil smile appeared on his face.
"I only need to talk to one of you... So I choose you, Tiger Mask... the rest, let’s dance." Kent moved, and a head burst open, blood spraying in the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 719: Pure Carnage [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent was often likened to a puppy by many.
He appeared harmless and funny. He seemed like someone who had been sheltered for years, given everything he needed without having to work for it.
He was that harmless, and if you didn’t truly know him, you would completely underestimate him. However, that was one thing Kent knew he could capitalize on to overwhelm his foes if he wanted.
Those who underestimated him would be crushed, and right now, the people he had been waiting for had arrived, bringing with them 170 men.
Kent planned on killing them all to send a message. He had already sent two messages to the Hand, but it seemed they didn’t listen, so this time, he would crush them thoroughly.
That was why he didn’t use his sword, but his fist.

Kent wasn’t even using his bloodline. After the two new limits broke on his mind and soul, he felt stronger than ever, so using his bare fists, he started killing, making sure the brutality that followed was one everyone would feel.
The first person’s head exploded like a watermelon, spraying blood into the air, but Kent didn’t stop to sympathize with him; he moved to the next and landed a punch on his chest.
*CHAWK*
His heart exploded inside, causing blood to flow from his mouth, eyes, and ears. He slowly fell to the ground. However, before he landed, Kent sent three more to escort him to the afterlife.

He punched a hole into one’s ribs, one lost half his face, and the other lost his head entirely. The sheer brutality Kent was unleashing left King Thalirion, the ten elders, the Half-Elf guards, Lady Aelith, the elven warriors, and the Tiger Fang in a state of shock.
Kent used the third skill he received from Vari to lock him down. It was a skill that did only one thing: to lock down an opponent, provided his soul was stronger than theirs.
Naturally, Kent’s Tier 13 soul and Tiger Fang’s Tier 11 soul had a significant gap that Tiger Fang could not compensate for, regardless of the treasure he used.
So Kent was superior to him.
And so he had locked him down, rendering him a mere statue forced to watch as hundreds of his men died in some of the most gruesome ways possible.
The [Statue] skill left him frozen in place, but his emotions were left untouched, causing him the pain Kent intended to inflict on him.
As for Lady Aelith, Kent planned on using the skill he received from Velyra to overwhelm her senses and make her humiliate herself.
Kent had no plans to kill her... Even his plan to kill the elven warriors was scrapped since he saw no value in it.
If he started killing just anyone, the Elves could alert all their men outside and in the Ancient Battlefield of Parting. Their orders would be to kill any human or Half-Elf they saw.
They could even go as far as ordering them to hunt them down, knowing full well Kent wouldn’t be able to save everyone, even if he were resourceful.
Though he might be able to save the Half-Elves now, those outside would pay the price. Kent didn’t want that, so instead of angering the Elves further, he planned on teaching them a lesson.
If possible, he wanted them to acknowledge the Half-Elves, for he knew soon enough they would rise, and when they did, they would fight back, leading to a more catastrophic ending for everyone.
But if he lets the elves go, none of that would happen, and before he ascends, the Half-Elves will become powerhouses. So peace now, peace forever.
Kent saw the hell Chaos had to go through to save his world from people who didn’t care about the common folk, just like the Hand was doing.
So Kent planned to purge them, but he also wanted a peaceful world where others could live, thrive, and grow in peace.
Killing the Elves wasn’t the right way to foster peace. And while he may be chaotic, he wasn’t a maniac who would go about killing just anyone.
The Hand was his target, and since they didn’t care who they hurt to get what they wanted, he also wouldn’t care who he killed to get what he wanted.
In under ten minutes, Kent slaughtered 70% of the Hand warriors. His hands were dyed red, his shirt, face, and hair painted red, showing he wasn’t planning on putting on a puppy face any longer.
’A bunch of weaklings think they have what it takes to suppress me. Do you even know who I am or where I came from?
I already told you I have what it takes to bring your organization to its knees, yet you treated it like a joke, thinking I’m like the weaklings you preyed on.
Open your eyes, bitches. Big Daddy Kent is no weakling, and I will show you all after I kill every last one of you."
As the words flowed from his mouth, his killing speed increased.
Bang! Crack!
Bang! Pow!
Bang! Chawk!
Every punch was either exploding heads, cracking bones, or rupturing internal organs. It was surgical-precision brutal killing—something the Hand warriors had no idea they would face.
But who could blame them? Kent had essentially relived years of memories from his life, fighting with his fists and claws.
That was something they could never understand; nobody could. And that is what made him dangerous.
Someone who grows stronger by simply remembering his past is no warrior weaklings can face.
The current Kent had no issues killing those three realms above him. He could handle Spirit Ascension stage experts, Spirit Kings, and even Spirit Emperors.

Perhaps Spirit Sovereigns would prove a headache depending on their level, and Spirit Lords were still out of his league. But even so, Kent was no easy opponent, so facing a bunch of Core Formation Experts was just bullying.
But he didn’t care. After fifteen minutes, the last head exploded, splashing blood on Kent one last time. Kent smirked, watching the blood stain his hand.
"Vexthra will bathe me," Kent smiled and walked toward Tiger Fang, grinning like an accomplished killer.
"And there is one remaining... I wonder what I should do with you."

Do you even know who I am or where I came from?
I already told you I have what it takes to bring your organization to its knees, yet you treated it like a joke, thinking I’m like the weaklings you preyed on.
Open your eyes, bitches.
Big Daddy Kent is no weakling, and I will show you all after I kill every last one of you."
As the words flowed from his mouth, his killing speed increased.
Bang!
Crack!
Bang!
Pow!
Bang!
Chawk!
Every punch was either exploding heads, cracking bones, or rupturing internal organs.
It was surgical-precision brutal killing—something the Hand warriors had no idea they would face.
But who could blame them?
Kent had essentially relived years of memories from his life, fighting with his fists and claws.
That was something they could never understand; nobody could.
And that is what made him dangerous.
Someone who grows stronger by simply remembering his past is no warrior weaklings can face.
The current Kent had no issues killing those three realms above him.
He could handle Spirit Ascension stage experts, Spirit Kings, and even Spirit Emperors.
Perhaps Spirit Sovereigns would prove a headache depending on their level, and Spirit Lords were still out of his league.
But even so, Kent was no easy opponent, so facing a bunch of Core Formation Experts was just bullying.
But he didn’t care.
After fifteen minutes, the last head exploded, splashing blood on Kent one last time.
Kent smirked, watching the blood stain his hand.
"Vexthra will bathe me," Kent smiled and walked toward Tiger Fang, grinning like an accomplished killer.
"And there is one remaining...
I wonder what I should do with you."

chapters.title: Chapter 720: Blade Whisperer
paragraphs: Kent locked eyes with the tiger-masked man for a few seconds before ripping the mask off his face. The moment the mask came off, gasps spread across the space.
The Elven warriors, Lady Aelith, King Thalirion, the elders, and the guards at the door gasped in unison. This prompted Kent to scan him. When he did, his eyes widened.
"Looks like you’re famous, Kenji, or should I call you the Blade Whisperer... the most wanted criminal/assassin of the world." Kent smiled as Kenji’s expression shifted from anger to fear.
Kent didn’t even bother paying attention to that, since he was busy reading about the crimes the scum before him had committed many years ago, but had never been caught for.

"Please tell me I’m not seeing things, but did he just unmask the true face of crime, the one that caused several powerhouses to remain indoors 1,200 years ago?" Lord Zaltarish asked, sounding even more scared as he spoke.
"What does this mean?"
"What do we do?"
"I mean, he was the one responsible for the poisoning, right... the one that left our Queen bedridden for a thousand years now?"

King Thalirion clenched his fist, staring at the man Kent had under lockdown, unsure of what to do. He had spent 400 years hunting this man, not to kill him but to get an antidote, one he needed to cure the poison in his wife.
One thousand two hundred years ago, King Thalirion was just crowned King of the Half-Elven race after their previous king used the tribulation to ascend to a higher world.
That day, when everything was reaching a climax, the Blade Whisperer, one of the most dangerous assassins in the world, struck.
He came for the new king, planning to end his legacy before it even began. However, he couldn’t kill the king because his dagger never reached him.
Instead, it pierced the Queen, who willingly threw herself at the blade laced with the most potent poison known to man.

Since then, the queen has been bedridden, barely alive thanks to an artifact the Dwarves used to protect her heart. Of course, such an evil assassin wouldn’t reveal the ingredients of his poison, so even after spending billions to hire Pill Kings, they couldn’t do anything.

Their only hope was to reach the Pill Emperor; that was their only chance. So for the past 1,000 years, the Half-Elves had been trying to send their best and brightest to the Supreme Immortal Sect in the hope they could reach the unreachable Pill Emperor—or, in this context, Pill Empress.
However, to this day, they have been unable to make any headway.

So, watching the cause of their decline and the reason the Elves fiercely tried to suppress the Half-Elves, King Thalirion didn’t know what even to do...His anger is boiling to the point that he could make a rational decision.
Kent read through the various crimes of the Blade Whisperer before turning to look at the King, whose fists were clenched, blood dripping—it was clear he was barely holding himself back.
Kent sighed and sent a message to Vexthra before speaking to the King.
"Being angry doesn’t look good on you, King Thalirion. I will cure your wife after I handle this scum."

Under normal circumstances, Kent’s words could be dismissed when he claimed he could cure what Pill Kings couldn’t. However, knowing what Kent had already done for them, the King paused for a few seconds and nodded.

"Good one," Kent smiled, then turned back to Tiger Fang. "You are one nasty individual, Mr. Tiger. It turns out everyone wants you dead—and here I thought I would spare your life." Kent shook his head with a smile that was both amused and furious.
"Right now, I won’t kill you myself, but you’re going to wish I did." Kent turned to Lady Aelith.
"I know you came thinking I was some weakling you could prey on. But here’s the thing, young lady: I may be 21 years old, but I have more than enough strength to kill hundreds of you.

However, I was raised by a woman this universe doesn’t deserve, so I will let you go. I know enough to know you are someone important to your people, so go back and be sure to tell your people the Half-Elves are off-limits.

From today onwards, they will start to rise, and there is nothing any of you can do to stop them. Of course, you might say, ’What happens after I leave? What then can they do when you come back?" Kent laughed and snapped his fingers.
Suddenly, Tribe Chief Malthar, Elder Ureth, Elder Farra, and Elder Zarka appeared, unleashing their overwhelming auras, which pushed everyone back, except for Kent.
Kent smiled, watching the public display of dominance. After the four new arrivals withdrew their aura, Kent spoke.
"Welcome to Elarion, Tribe Chief Malthar, Elder Ureth, Farra, and Zarka..."
"It’s good to be here, Kent. This place is nice... not that it’s anywhere close to where we live... It’s just good to be outside," Tribe Chief Malthar said with a smile.
"We’ll talk about that later," Kent laughed and turned back to Lady Aelith. "From what I know, the Elves and Half-Elves were once allies... so what happened? Why can’t that be a thing anymore?
Well, I don’t care... Just know that these four are looking to ally with the Half-Elves, and in case you have any plans to be arrogant, why don’t you hear what the imposing one has to say?"
Tribe Chief Malthar stepped forward. "I see you’re also a warrior, so you can call me Malthar. I am the tribe chief of the Bloodvein tribe, from the Dead Region."
Everyone who heard him widened their eyes, unsure of what to think.

The Dead Region—one of the most dangerous places in the Ancient Battlefield of Parting, a place no sane person dares to go. Now, there are not one but four people from that place standing before them...
What does that mean?
What does that say to them...
"You heard the man... He and his tribe are now willing to ally with the Half-Elves, meaning they now have the backing not just of me, but of a tribe from the Dead Region.

I know you are wise, young lady, so be sure to make the right choice, because while I don’t want to become enemies of the Elves, I also can wipe you out just like you did with the High Elves." Kent winked at Lady Aelith, whose body shuddered and face turned pale.
"Now, back to you, Mr. Tiger. How do you want to die?"

chapters.title: Chapter 721: Fate Of The Hunter
paragraphs: What Kent saw when he scanned Kenji was just too horrific. He is wanted by the Dragons, Elves, Beasts, Dwarves, Half-Elves, and even the Demons.
To be wanted by the demons means a lot...
His crimes are just too numerous, and from the first few Kent read, he couldn’t bring himself to think that a person could be this evil.
⟦Name: Kenji Namota⟧
⟦Title: The Blade Whisperer | Tiger Fang⟧
⟦Race: Tigerkin⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (7/7)⟧
⟦Affiliation: The Hand⟧
↠ The Blade Whisperer, one of the deadliest assassins to ever grace the people of Sonox with his evil means of assassination. All his kills were horrific and disturbing.
↠ The only assassin whom everyone knows but nobody was able to do anything to. His reputation precedes him, and that is why he is the most wanted man in the world.
↠ The Dragon Emperor wanted him for the brutal assassination of his only daughter, who had not even begun cultivating.
↠ He poisoned the sacred waters of the Elven Kingdom, causing countless deaths and a famine that lasted three hundred years.
↠ He slaughtered an entire caravan of beast tamers, sparing no one, including children and the elderly. Some of these children were the maids of the children of nobles, whom he wanted to kill.
↠ He infiltrated the Dwarven stronghold and destroyed their ancient forge, crippling their ability to produce weapons for decades.
↠ He ambushed the Half-Elves’ crowning ceremony and tried to assassinate the new king, but ended up injuring the Queen instead.
↠ He unleashed a cursed plague upon a demon village, turning its inhabitants into mindless monsters. The town had to be purged, which cost the lives of 240,000 people living in the village
↠ He assassinated the brother of the current leader of Beastkins during a sacred ceremony, defiling their most holy ground.

Kenji Namota is not merely a killer; he is a force of destruction whose evil touches every corner of the world. His list of carnage was so extensive that Kent would have to read everything during his free time.
However, for now, while Kenji was the evil everyone wanted dead, Kent had a much different plan for him.
Kent first used ’Soul Torture’, allowing him to take hold of his mind. Then he began his evil killing plan...
"Contact your leader." Kent gave him a command.
Kenji did as he was told. He took out his communication crystal and channeled his energy into it...
The moment the lazy voice of their leader sounded from the crystal, Kent smiled.
"I don’t believe we’ve officially met, lady... I am Kent Madson, and while you can’t see me, whatever you think of me, it is probably true. I am that handsome.
Anyway, I didn’t call to tell you how handsome I am. The reason for the call is to tell you in person that you’ve been a great disappointment.
I expected a result. I expected you to have already opened the gates... but what did I get? A bunch of weaklings who couldn’t even withstand a single punch.
Not that I expected much from an organization that calls itself ’The Hand.’ I mean, what kind of idiot names their organization ’The Hand’? It’s just stupid.
However, I suppose it suits you, so if that makes you sleep at night, then I’ll be happy to call you the ’Hand.’
Before I trail off, know that the next batch you send my way will all die, so heed my advice and invest your time in searching for the keys.

Get all seven and execute your big, bad plan. I will be there waiting to stop whatever walks through those gates. Basically, as long as I am alive, whatever you have planned will never come to fruition.
Anyway, you can go back to work now. I have to kill the one with the tiger mask. It turns out he was a wanted man in not one, but multiple kingdoms.
Talk to you later..."
With that, Kent stopped talking and crushed the communication crystal. His focus turned to Kenji, and then a grin appeared on Kent’s face.
"Killing you with my own hands would be a waste, so why don’t you do it yourself? Since you like killing, please try this on yourself.

You have seven minutes to cut yourself ten thousand times, but you are not allowed to scream or cry. Also, before the seven minutes are over, you cannot die. And please, I will count—so ten thousand cuts, painful but no tears, bloody but no screams. You can start now."
The command was absolute. There was no fighting it.
So, under the horrified gaze of everyone around, Kenji drew his dagger and started cutting himself. He began with his left arm, slicing wounds into it as he gritted his teeth.
Deep within, he wanted to stop. He tried to scream; he wanted to cry. But the command Kent gave him was meant for torture, something Kent wished to use only on the scum of society.
He wanted to make them bleed, feel the pain deep within, and try their best to resist, but in the end, they would succumb, unable to withstand the torture.
So when Kent gave the order, he was prepared to become evil to punish evil.
"Get creative, Kenji. Your handsome face is there; your nice hair is there... I need to see a bloody face, a bloody scalp, and a severed nose.
Become the Joker—cut that mouth of yours open. Get creative, Kenji, or I’ll be forced to do it for you.
Prove to everyone you are the Blade Whisperer, the Tiger Fang... show them how creative you are. Make them believe you have what it takes to terrorize kingdoms."
As Kent spoke more commands, Kenji continued to bleed, feeling his energy drain, but he couldn’t stop—not when he was nowhere close to the ten thousand cuts Kent demanded.
Kenji cut his mouth wide open, causing most of the elves to turn away. They could feel his pain; they could feel that tear in their own mouths, and the sensation was one they weren’t prepared for.
Lady Aelith looked at Kent intensely, her face pale as she imagined herself in Kenji’s place. The thought alone made her shudder.

’This human, I am not crossing him ever again. If possible, I would prefer not to see him again. I will run... no, I will enter seclusion as soon as I return. That is, if he let me leave with my life’
She made her plan. She would rather run into hiding than risk another chance of staring Kent in the eye. The Chaos Dragon scared her shitless.

chapters.title: Chapter 722: Point Made.
paragraphs: Under the horrified gaze of everyone present, Kenji, a once-menacing figure who had harmed thousands, took his last slash before collapsing onto the ground, dead.
Seven minutes—that was how long it took him to cut himself ten thousand times. It was a horrific display, one that shook everyone to the core.
Kent, of course, remained emotionless, almost as if he hadn’t terrified everyone. Even Tribe Chief Malthar and his elders, who are faithful followers of the Mother of Killers, were visibly shaken.

It was supposed to be death by a thousand cuts. However, Kent had transformed it into death by ten thousand cuts. Worse still, instead of being inflicted by others, the cuts were self-inflicted, intensifying the horror.
That was just too horrifying, and judging by everyone’s expressions, it was clear they were terrified of Kent—really terrified.
Kent looked at the corpse on the ground for a few seconds before a sigh escaped his lips. "You died too easily."
’Did he just say that bastard died too easily? Was that not horrifying and evil enough?’ Lady Aelith wondered, visibly frightened by the human standing not far from her.
’For someone who claims to be only twenty-one years old, this level of savagery is far too much. What happens when he turns a hundred, or even a thousand years old?’ King Thalirion wondered.
If only they knew Kent could have done far worse. What he had shown was merely the tip of the iceberg.
Jest gave him knowledge of the sword. His understanding had deepened, and now he could boldly claim that his knowledge of the sword surpassed that of most Sword Kings.
Such was the benefit of being the best swordsman ever to walk the face of the universe.
Then Chaos taught him how to harness his strength, tap into his bloodline, and unleash chaos upon his enemies. The brutality of his bloodline originated from Chaos.

However, from Jaqen, the Faceless Assassin, Kent gained insight into killing methods. He only recalled a tiny fraction of the assassin’s memories, so Kent didn’t fully know that life, but he had seen enough to understand how to kill someone quietly, either painlessly or painfully.
Jaqen’s memories weren’t exactly pleasant, so Kent learned all the twisted methods of killing, and today, he had unleashed one of them. Surprisingly, it worked like a charm.
Now, he could only hope that more opportunities like this would present themselves, allowing him to showcase his brutality.
Kent turned to Lady Aelith.

"You can leave. But heed my words: the next time you and your kind come against me or the Half-Elves, there will be hell to pay. Now, you can go. Please, when you see me in your kingdom, do not send me packing."
"I was told the Elves are skilled in alchemy, and as it turns out, I am also an alchemist. I might come there to buy some things."
"That will be all. Once again, you are free to go."
Kent turned and faced King Thalirion and the elders. "I will be back in an hour. But for now, you can have some discussions with Tribe Chief Malthar and his elders."
"I’m sure something good will come out of it."
The king nodded. Kent vanished from where he stood and appeared in the Harem Tower. The moment he did, Vexthra and Princess Lovina appeared.
"Wow, what happened to you?" Princess Lovina asked, staring at Kent’s bloody appearance. He was painted red from head to toe, looking more like a blood demon than a human.
Kent smiled. "I had a couple of guys over for a sparring session. Turns out they weren’t that strong. One punch, and they couldn’t even keep their heads on their bodies. They disappointed me."
Kent shook his head like an ancestor disappointed in his descendants after returning from a million years in seclusion.
Vexthra and Lovina shook their heads, watching the man’s smug behavior.
"Come on, you need to clean up." They led Kent straight to the bathing room, where they stripped him naked and began bathing him.
It took several minutes, but eventually, the blood washed off his body, and after some more cleaning, he was squeaky clean.
They then took him from the bathtub and placed him in a sauna, where Vexthra began giving Little Kent some much-needed attention. Princess Lovina, meanwhile, was ensuring Kent’s muscles relaxed.
Of course, she was next in line to make sure Little Kent felt their love. Thankfully, only the two of them had come this time, giving them more than enough time to ensure Kent fully relaxed.
And so, they did.
After giving Kent fellatio for four good hours, Vexthra climbed onto him and rode the midnight train for two hours before Princess Lovina took over and did her best to make Kent moan.
After fourteen hours, Kent managed to calm down and fell asleep in the arms of his two loving wives. Eight hours later, he woke up feeling refreshed and ready to face the day.
"Lovina, my love, you and Vexthra will be escorting me to Elarion. I need your help with something," Kent said, and Princess Lovina nodded.

sentences.text: Under the horrified gaze of everyone present, Kenji, a once-menacing figure who had harmed thousands, took his last slash before collapsing onto the ground, dead.
Seven minutes—that was how long it took him to cut himself ten thousand times.
It was a horrific display, one that shook everyone to the core.
Kent, of course, remained emotionless, almost as if he hadn’t terrified everyone.
Even Tribe Chief Malthar and his elders, who are faithful followers of the Mother of Killers, were visibly shaken.
It was supposed to be death by a thousand cuts.
However, Kent had transformed it into death by ten thousand cuts.
Worse still, instead of being inflicted by others, the cuts were self-inflicted, intensifying the horror.
That was just too horrifying, and judging by everyone’s expressions, it was clear they were terrified of Kent—really terrified.
Kent looked at the corpse on the ground for a few seconds before a sigh escaped his lips.
"You died too easily."
’Did he just say that bastard died too easily?
Was that not horrifying and evil enough?’ Lady Aelith wondered, visibly frightened by the human standing not far from her.
’For someone who claims to be only twenty-one years old, this level of savagery is far too much.
What happens when he turns a hundred, or even a thousand years old?’ King Thalirion wondered.
If only they knew Kent could have done far worse.
What he had shown was merely the tip of the iceberg.
Jest gave him knowledge of the sword.
His understanding had deepened, and now he could boldly claim that his knowledge of the sword surpassed that of most Sword Kings.
Such was the benefit of being the best swordsman ever to walk the face of the universe.
Then Chaos taught him how to harness his strength, tap into his bloodline, and unleash chaos upon his enemies.
The brutality of his bloodline originated from Chaos.
However, from Jaqen, the Faceless Assassin, Kent gained insight into killing methods.
He only recalled a tiny fraction of the assassin’s memories, so Kent didn’t fully know that life, but he had seen enough to understand how to kill someone quietly, either painlessly or painfully.
Jaqen’s memories weren’t exactly pleasant, so Kent learned all the twisted methods of killing, and today, he had unleashed one of them.
Surprisingly, it worked like a charm.
Now, he could only hope that more opportunities like this would present themselves, allowing him to showcase his brutality.

"You can leave.
But heed my words: the next time you and your kind come against me or the Half-Elves, there will be hell to pay.

"That will be all.

Turns out they weren’t that strong.
One punch, and they couldn’t even keep their heads on their bodies.
They disappointed me."

Vexthra and Lovina shook their heads, watching the man’s smug behavior.

Of course, she was next in line to make sure Little Kent felt their love.
Thankfully, only the two of them had come this time, giving them more than enough time to ensure Kent fully relaxed.
And so, they did.
