chapters.title: Chapter 735: The Competition (3)
paragraphs: Kent looked at the blue-haired, handsome young man named Laith before him and smiled. Of course, he planned not to use the arrows again.
During the battles he observed, he developed several skills and planned to utilize them effectively. He was able to master those skills simply by observing the contestants’ battle.
So he knew he wouldn’t overwhelm his opponents again if he used their own skills against them.
"Begin."
The moment the order was given, the blue-haired half-Elf conjured a giant scythe and slashed it at Kent. It was made from red flame, so as the scythe moved, a trail of crimson fire followed it.
However, Kent stood there watching the scythe close in. When it was a few meters from him, he snapped his fingers, and a shield appeared.
The moment the shield appeared, Ember, the red-haired beauty who fought first in the first round, widened her eyes.
"That is my flame skill. He is using my skill."

Others noticed this, too. However, what shocked them was that when the scythe landed on the shield, instead of a whirlwind of infernal energy emerging from the shield like Ember’s skill, ten tendrils appeared and shot at Laith.
Standing among the contestants, a young lady named Josselin narrowed her eyes when the tendrils appeared.
"That is my ’Dancing Tendrils’ skill. How did he merge my skill with Ember’s skills?"
But Kent wasn’t done. The moment the tendrils latched onto Laith, a lotus bloomed beneath Laith and exploded, sending him flying off the stage.
Adrie stood among the contestants, her face in a shocked expression. "That was my Exploding Lotus skill. How did he know how to use that?"
Up in the viewing area, Queen Jascia stared at Kent with a shocked expression. "Did he just use not one but three skills from three different people?"

The shocked expression on her face only deepened, knowing full well that was what had happened. Kent indeed used the skills of his fellow contestants. He mastered all their skills to the point that he could use all of them without any issue.
"Is that even possible?" Princess Elowen, seated beside her mother, asked, also looking in Kent’s direction with a shocked expression.
"Kent Madson, if you don’t mind, I have a question for you." The queen needed answers, so she asked, and Kent turned in her direction.
"I don’t mind, my Queen," Kent said with a straight face.
"The skills you just used—were they copied from your fellow contestants?" the queen asked, and Kent nodded, dumbfounding everyone.
"I am sorry if that was offensive. However, after my first battle, I realized that my skills are not suited for friendly fighting like this.
All the skills I possess are for killing, but I am not here to traumatize anyone. This was why I had to get creative and tone things down a bit, so I copied a few skills.
And I have to say, these skills have potential." Kent paused and turned to the people whose skills he copied.
"I am sorry if my actions offended you."
Both the queen, the contestants, and the audience could only stare at Kent with expressions of shock.
Queen Jascia studied Kent’s expression for a few seconds and then nodded.

"You’ve done nothing bad, Kent. In battle, being able to learn your opponent’s moves is half the battle won. So, having the capabilities to copy the skills of your opponents in this contest shows you are not someone to underestimate."
She turned to the contestants. "This is a lesson to you all. Sometimes, you will meet people like him. People who don’t follow the same rules as we do. They are monsters beyond our comprehension.
People who will do things that don’t align with common sense—things like copying your skills and using them more effectively than you.
However, instead of feeling offended, you should instead grab this opportunity and learn from him, for you never know when he will be leaving." The queen smiled.
"In other words, all of you should show him your skills in the contest and let him help you gain a better understanding of them. Don’t waste this opportunity.
And that is your punishment for stealing other people’s skills, Kent Madson." Kent smiled, hearing how shameless the queen sounded.
She never failed to secure an opportunity for her people.
"I will do my best to handle my punishment with dignity, my Queen," Kent responded.
"You better."
Kent walked away, and the queen leaned back in her chair. After a few seconds, she turned to Princess Elowen.
"I need his genes."

Princess Elowen widened her eyes, then a blush appeared on her face, causing her to turn away. "Oh, don’t be a baby, Elowen. He is a perfect gentleman to have some babies with. So what do you say—two daughters and a son... That will be enough for me."
"Mom..." Princess Elowen’s blush deepened. She turned to her father to come to her rescue, but the king just smiled, shaking his head.

"Your mother is not wrong, though. That handsome human has all the qualities of a good husband." And just like that, Princess Elowen was forced to run out of the room to calm her nerves, leaving her two parents to laugh at her predicament.
"She is still a baby," Queen Jascia said.
"She is over a thousand years old, but I guess she is still a baby."
The remaining battles happened after Kent’s dominance. After every last battle was fought, only 551 remained.
Those who washed out received their gifts with smiles on their faces. After the second round, they were given two two-hour breaks to recover before the third round.
During the recovery period, Kent used the time to document all the spies he had identified, providing sufficient evidence to support his claim.
He knew that after the king and the elders reviewed his documents, they would confirm that every last one of the spies he had discovered was indeed true.
After resting, Lord Yael appeared again to tell them how the third round would happen.
Also, at this rate, the allure of walking home with a Mythic Grade Ambrosia apple and a 10,000-year-old Soul Cleansing Berry made all those who qualified for the third round more than happy.
"The third stage will see only ten of you qualifying..." Lord Yael began.

The shocked expression on her face only deepened, knowing full well that was what had happened.
Kent indeed used the skills of his fellow contestants.
He mastered all their skills to the point that he could use all of them without any issue.
"Is that even possible?" Princess Elowen, seated beside her mother, asked, also looking in Kent’s direction with a shocked expression.
"Kent Madson, if you don’t mind, I have a question for you." The queen needed answers, so she asked, and Kent turned in her direction.
"I don’t mind, my Queen," Kent said with a straight face.
"The skills you just used—were they copied from your fellow contestants?" the queen asked, and Kent nodded, dumbfounding everyone.
"I am sorry if that was offensive.
However, after my first battle, I realized that my skills are not suited for friendly fighting like this.
All the skills I possess are for killing, but I am not here to traumatize anyone.
This was why I had to get creative and tone things down a bit, so I copied a few skills.
And I have to say, these skills have potential." Kent paused and turned to the people whose skills he copied.
"I am sorry if my actions offended you."
Both the queen, the contestants, and the audience could only stare at Kent with expressions of shock.
Queen Jascia studied Kent’s expression for a few seconds and then nodded.
"You’ve done nothing bad, Kent.
In battle, being able to learn your opponent’s moves is half the battle won.
So, having the capabilities to copy the skills of your opponents in this contest shows you are not someone to underestimate."
She turned to the contestants.
"This is a lesson to you all.
Sometimes, you will meet people like him.
People who don’t follow the same rules as we do.
They are monsters beyond our comprehension.
People who will do things that don’t align with common sense—things like copying your skills and using them more effectively than you.
However, instead of feeling offended, you should instead grab this opportunity and learn from him, for you never know when he will be leaving." The queen smiled.
"In other words, all of you should show him your skills in the contest and let him help you gain a better understanding of them.
Don’t waste this opportunity.
And that is your punishment for stealing other people’s skills, Kent Madson." Kent smiled, hearing how shameless the queen sounded.
She never failed to secure an opportunity for her people.
"I will do my best to handle my punishment with dignity, my Queen," Kent responded.
"You better."
Kent walked away, and the queen leaned back in her chair.
After a few seconds, she turned to Princess Elowen.
"I need his genes."
Princess Elowen widened her eyes, then a blush appeared on her face, causing her to turn away.
"Oh, don’t be a baby, Elowen.
He is a perfect gentleman to have some babies with.
So what do you say—two daughters and a son...
That will be enough for me."
"Mom..." Princess Elowen’s blush deepened.
She turned to her father to come to her rescue, but the king just smiled, shaking his head.
"Your mother is not wrong, though.

That handsome human has all the qualities of a good husband." And just like that, Princess Elowen was forced to run out of the room to calm her nerves, leaving her two parents to laugh at her predicament.
"She is still a baby," Queen Jascia said.
"She is over a thousand years old, but I guess she is still a baby."
The remaining battles happened after Kent’s dominance.
After every last battle was fought, only 551 remained.
Those who washed out received their gifts with smiles on their faces.
After the second round, they were given two two-hour breaks to recover before the third round.
During the recovery period, Kent used the time to document all the spies he had identified, providing sufficient evidence to support his claim.
He knew that after the king and the elders reviewed his documents, they would confirm that every last one of the spies he had discovered was indeed true.
After resting, Lord Yael appeared again to tell them how the third round would happen.
Also, at this rate, the allure of walking home with a Mythic Grade Ambrosia apple and a 10,000-year-old Soul Cleansing Berry made all those who qualified for the third round more than happy.
"The third stage will see only ten of you qualifying..." Lord Yael began.

chapters.title: Chapter 736: The Competition (4) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The stage was transformed for the third round.
Now, instead of a fighting stage, a glass chamber was set on the stage. Within the chamber lay ten crystals. A quick scan revealed they were flame crystals.
Kent could see a few holes in the glass, which allowed air to flow into the chamber. It also had some runic engravings on parts of the glass and the crystals.

"The third round is simple. All you have to do is use your flames to pick as many flame crystals as you can. Know that every last crystal has runes that make them ten times heavier, so be careful with the amount of energy you put into it.
That said, you should stop if you can’t go any further.
Of course, this round will be judged by how many crystals you can pick up and how long you manage to hold them.
You might qualify to be part of the top ten, so exhausting yourself will lower your chances of passing the next trial, which also requires you to have enough energy to pass."
Everyone nodded, and Lord Yael gestured for the third round to start.
The first person to be called was Madea. Her number appeared on the board, so she moved toward the glass chamber.
"How many do you think she will be able to pick?" one person asked in the audience.

"Knowing her, I say she can go as far as seven, maybe eight. Her control of the flame element is natural. And considering her mother is one of the most powerful flame users, I don’t see her failing this trial easily."
"I guess we will see what she is capable of in a few seconds."
"I guess so, too."
Madea stopped in front of the glass chamber and turned to the instructor overseeing this third round.
"Whenever you are ready," the instructor said.
Madea studied the setup for a few minutes before channeling her flame energy. Her blue flame surged and immediately wrapped around five stones, lifting them off the glass floor.
However, she wasn’t done; she surged her fire further, wrapping it around the sixth, taking it off the glass surface. She then went for the seventh, slowly taking it off the glassy floor.

At this rate, everyone could tell she was having some difficulty going further. But she went for the eighth, and after some struggle, she managed to raise that one for a few seconds—enough to record—before all eight stones fell.
Madea gasped for breath as her fans cheered for her, filling the arena with their happiness. Lifting eight crystals was something that couldn’t be easily achieved, yet Madea was able to do it.
Her name appeared on the ranking, earning her a spot at the top. The second contestant was called next, and she also managed to lift seven crystals.

Of course, she attempted to go for the eighth crystal, but she just couldn’t. Taking Lord Yael’s advice, she didn’t force herself to go for the eighth, knowing full well that doing so would require a day or perhaps two days of rest before she could use her fire effectively again.
More were called, but the highest anyone reached was seven crystals. Kent sat on one side, watching them all with a calm expression.

In his mind, though, he knew this trial was meant for an alchemist. Only an alchemist could pass this trial to perfection because, while the crystals were heavy, he had held pills inside a cauldron many times, so he knew if he pushed a little, just lifting ten flame crystals would be possible.

Eventually, it was Norion, the other genius number, that appeared on the board. He swaggered to the glass chamber with his shoulders held high. He stopped and looked at the crystals, just as every last one of those who came before him did.
Then his flame surged, wrapping around six crystals instantly.
’Show off,’ Kent said inwardly.
’Taking six at once will hinder him from going beyond eight. This is like going to the gym for the first time. Instead of aiming for 60kg on the first day, start with 10kg and gradually build up.’
He sighed and watched as Norion wrapped his flame around the seventh crystal and slowly took it up. He struggled for a moment, but she managed to lift the crystal.

Then he went for the eighth crystal, which, just like Madea’s, required him to use more of his flame energy. It took some grunting and straining, but he managed to lift it, earning praise from those around him.
Naturally, he wasn’t at his limit, but if he were to go further, he would have exhausted his energy.
But he managed to lift eight flame crystals, so that was enough to set him atop those who went before him.

More went after him, but aside from him and Madea, none managed to lift eight crystals. Of course, the next genius who went managed to take eight, but he might have just wasted too much energy. However, he seemed not to mind.
By the time the last of the five geniuses went, Kent noticed the rivalry between them. They were competing against each other, so each tried their best to lift the 8th crystal.
Not that he cared about that. As long as it wasn’t something that would compromise their future, nobody really cared about their rivalry.
Having rivalries is another way to grow as a cultivator.
Of course, that is normal and, in a way, even healthy.
Even companies back on Earth have competitions they battle with, especially in the tech industry, so this harmless rivalry was warranted.
Kent was called after 540 had their turn. The moment he started moving toward the flame chamber, the audience began speculating how many he could lift.
"I say he can lift all ten. He has already shown us he is a genius among geniuses."
"I think so, too. But he will have to put in some effort if he wants to go for all ten."

"That is only normal. I heard the Supreme Immortal Sect has a similar setup, but a crystal is thirty times heavier, and you are required to lift at least three before you can proceed to the next exam.
So far, only five of our people have come close to achieving that. So perhaps this human can make a difference."
Kent stopped before the glass chamber.

chapters.title: Chapter 737: The Competition (5)
paragraphs: Kent looked intently at the glass chamber and sighed. ’At this rate, people will think I am just showing off. However, they never knew all these trials were as simple as they could be to me.’
He had merely breezed through the first two, and standing before the third, he couldn’t help shaking his head.
His golden flame surged.
Inside the glass chamber, Kent’s golden flame slowly wrapped around the first flame crystal and calmly lifted it off the glassy floor. The lift was slow but fluid.

Of course, everyone became puzzled when Kent didn’t immediately wrap his flame around five crystals and lift them off the ground like those who came before him. If he had done that, he would have earned some cheers.
However, what he received were questions about whether he would be able to complete the third trial.
"I think we might have made an error in placing him among the top five geniuses. He couldn’t even lift five flame crystals at once. That is just disappointing."
"I don’t think we should be quick to judge. Look at him, it wasn’t like he was struggling at all. If anything, we should watch him to the end to determine."
"I hope he doesn’t wash out early."
Kent wrapped his energy around the second crystal, just as he had with the first, and lifted it. Then, he approached the third.

’Of course, I could have gone for all ten crystals, but this is a lesson to the four that will be joining me to enter the Tower and the sect. I can help them with the Flame Tower, but when it comes to the sect, I know nothing of that...yet’

’However, I overheard someone say that the sect has a similar trial to this one. So those who have eyes would see that lifting all the stones at once is such a bad idea.’ Kent sighed as he lifted the third into the air.

’The moment the stone is lifted off the ground by six inches, the rune stops affecting it, making it return to its original weight. However, all of them lifted it up to four inches, which is just too short.’
’However, if they had lifted it one by one, perhaps one of them would have recognized this. But now that I am doing this, I hope they learn from it, for I may not be generous in the future.’
Kent smiled as he lifted the fourth crystal.

The fifth followed, then the sixth. At this point, everyone was starting to see a trend in Kent’s trial. However, while their questions wanted to come out, they could only watch as Kent lifted the seventh and eighth crystals.
Then, when it came to the ninth, Kent paused and looked at Madea and the top geniuses before wrapping his flame around both the ninth and tenth, lifting them off the glass floor simultaneously.
The moment the tenth crystal was in the air, cheers rang out as everyone cheered Kent on. It was as if their dream of having someone from the Half-Elf Kingdom join the sect had come true.
They all cheered for Kent as he held the crystal aloft, his handsome face beaming with a smile.
After a full minute, he lowered the crystals before taking a deep sigh. ’It is strange how I didn’t even feel anything... like I never even used my flame essence.’

Kent walked off the stage under the watchful gaze of every last contestant. They knew he had proven to everyone he was the best, and at the same time, also proved he was the right person to make the dreams of every Half-Elf come to pass.

A few of the contestants—of course, the ones yet to go—had expressions of defeat on their faces. The five geniuses had already demonstrated their strength, and now that Kent had, they all began to wonder if they had a chance.
But of course, they wouldn’t have to think much deeper into it since the next person was called. With no reason to step down, the rest tried their luck, and in the end, only ten passed.
The ranking showed that Kent was first, followed by Madea in second, Norion in third, and the list continued from there.

Those who washed out were given their gift and left with satisfied expressions on their faces. Of course, they would have loved to be part of the ten remaining, but in the end, they couldn’t meet the expectations to be among the top ten.
However, among the top ten, five would also have to wash out.

There are only five slots, so only five of them will be entering the Flame Tower. They knew this, so when Lord Yael appeared to announce the last trial that would determine the winners, everyone except Kent tensed.
"We are almost at the point where we will be finding out the top five to represent the Half-Elves in the Flame Tower opening. This means that five of you won’t be able to enter the tower.
But as you all heard, our Queen announced that three years from now, we will have fifteen slots, so don’t be heartbroken if you couldn’t make it into the Flame Tower this time around.
However, I have something else to add. Upon a few deliberations, we decided to make the last trial the same as the third trial.
This means you will have to lift the crystals again, and points will be awarded based on how many you manage to lift and how long they remain off the glassy floor."
The moment Kent heard Lord Yael’s words, a smile appeared on his face. They were already warned not to exhaust their energies too much during the third round.
However, Kent knew most, if not all, of them had used more than they had now during the third round. This means they would struggle in the fourth round.
"Of course, since only five of you will be making it through, this means you can go all out. Even if you pass out, there won’t be another trial. But that said, don’t pass out..."

Lord Yael smiled at everyone before he moved away. On the board, the first person was called. Ember walked to the stage with a weak smile. She managed to enter the top ten, but she was already doubting her chances of being one of the top five.

chapters.title: Chapter 738: End of The Competition
paragraphs: None of the contestants, not even Kent, expected the last trial to be a repeat of the third trial. So this caught them off guard. However, since it was a decision made by the elders, there was no changing it, and so they had to comply.
Ember walked to the glass chamber and channeled her flame energy, wrapping it around three crystals just as she had in the third trial.
She managed to lift the crystals 4 inches off the glassy floor. However, she couldn’t move up to the 6-inch mark, which would have earned her some chance to go further than the last time.
But in the end, she made the same mistake as last time.

The 4th crystal was lifted off the glassy floor, followed by the 5th and 6th. However, it was some strain to raise the 7th and then the 8th, which in this case only lasted in the air for less than two seconds before dropping all eight.
Thankfully, she managed to earn eight counts. However, her breath turned ragged as she moved back with a smile on her face.
Physically, she was not exhausted. However, when it comes to matters of the soul, channeling too much of her soul flame essence isn’t just too dangerous but too taxing on the soul.
So it was more like soul exhaustion, one that can’t be recovered from quickly, compared to physical exhaustion. But since this was the final trial, she went all out, and it paid off.
The following number appeared, and the person walked forward. Just like Ember, he also made the same mistake, going all out from the start.

Watching this, Kent knew they hadn’t learned anything from his display. But who could blame them? They were merely fascinated by what he was able to accomplish, to the point that they failed to notice the patterns that emerged.

And so this mistake was repeated throughout the numbers that were called. Eventually, it was Norion’s turn. He was one of the five geniuses, so everyone was eagerly looking forward to his win over those who had come before him.
All four who went before him—three managed to lift eight crystals, while one only lifted seven crystals—so Norion had to do better than them.
He tried, making sure his failure didn’t stop him from lifting less than eight crystals. Thankfully, he managed to lift nine, albeit with sheer difficulty.
After him, Dorren went, and he also managed to lift nine, showing the rivalry wouldn’t let them relax when there was a slot to enter the flame tower on the line.

Madea followed and managed to lift nine crystals, even attempting the tenth, but she couldn’t. Shaking her head, she walked away, and Elia went to see if she, too, was destined to be among the top five.
In the end, she also managed to lift nine crystals. However, she wasn’t happy if one were to compare her achievement to those of Norion, Dorren, or Madea.
This meant that if Ostorious performed better than her, she would be the one to wash out, since there was no way Kent would fall behind any of them.
Kent had already lifted all ten crystals in the third trial, so she wasn’t banking on him to fail... so she could only hope Ostorious didn’t go beyond eight crystals.
Kent, of course, knew the outcome, but he just stood there as Ostorious’ turn came, and he walked to the glass chamber.
The moment Ostorious wrapped his energy around four crystals, Kent shook his head and smiled. Queen Jascia, who was paying attention to Kent, narrowed her gaze as the realization dawned on her.
"I think with him here, even if for a few days, these kids will gain more experience than they could ever dream of." Naturally, she made up her mind to add to Kent’s punishment.
Ostorious managed to lift seven crystals, but that was when he felt the exhaustion reach deep down into his soul.
When he lifted the eighth, he couldn’t go beyond that, and knowing he had already failed, he dropped the crystals and left with a defeated smile.
The last person to walk into the chamber was Kent. This time, he planned to show everyone that in the face of great strength and control, all planning is useless.

When he reached the glass chamber, he waved his hand, and his flame surged around all ten crystals. Then, with ease, he lifted all the crystals from the glassy floor and suspended them ten inches above the ground.
"So he faked the first trial," Princess Elowen, who had managed to recover and return inside during the third trial, asked her mother as she gazed intently at Kent.

"He didn’t fake it... He tried to show his fellow contestants something, but it seemed they failed to grasp it." Queen Elowen, who suspected Kent had discovered something about the trial, replied, already planning to know more.
"Why don’t you ask him, Mom?" Elowen said, but her mother smiled, "You can also ask him. After all, you will be walking hand in hand with him soon."
Princess Elowen looked at her mother for a few seconds before the words she had forgotten came to mind: "Shameless."
Her mother just smiled before turning to Kent, who was walking off the stage.

"Kent Madson, I saw how you completed the third trial just a couple of minutes ago, and I would say it is completely different from how the fourth trial was completed. Care to shed some light on that?"
Kent smiled, already expecting this when he felt the queen’s gaze on him. He expected her to ask such a question, so he prepared a good yet short answer.
"The reason my third trial was different from the fourth was that I tried to show my fellow contestants how to lift all the crystals easily.
It turns out that the moment the crystals are six inches off the ground, their weight returns to normal, meaning the rune around the crystals is ineffective when the crystals are that high.
This also means instead of spending ten times the effort and energy to hold the crystals in the air, you only need one-tenth of the effort.
In other words, holding the crystals six inches off the ground would save you more energy to lift the remaining crystals."
Every last contestant who participated in the third and fourth trials held their jaw, staring at Kent as he walked back to his spot with a smile on his face.

sentences.text: None of the contestants, not even Kent, expected the last trial to be a repeat of the third trial.
So this caught them off guard.
However, since it was a decision made by the elders, there was no changing it, and so they had to comply.
Ember walked to the glass chamber and channeled her flame energy, wrapping it around three crystals just as she had in the third trial.
She managed to lift the crystals 4 inches off the glassy floor.
However, she couldn’t move up to the 6-inch mark, which would have earned her some chance to go further than the last time.
But in the end, she made the same mistake as last time.
The 4th crystal was lifted off the glassy floor, followed by the 5th and 6th.
However, it was some strain to raise the 7th and then the 8th, which in this case only lasted in the air for less than two seconds before dropping all eight.
Thankfully, she managed to earn eight counts.
However, her breath turned ragged as she moved back with a smile on her face.
Physically, she was not exhausted.
However, when it comes to matters of the soul, channeling too much of her soul flame essence isn’t just too dangerous but too taxing on the soul.
So it was more like soul exhaustion, one that can’t be recovered from quickly, compared to physical exhaustion.
But since this was the final trial, she went all out, and it paid off.
The following number appeared, and the person walked forward.
Just like Ember, he also made the same mistake, going all out from the start.
Watching this, Kent knew they hadn’t learned anything from his display.
But who could blame them?
They were merely fascinated by what he was able to accomplish, to the point that they failed to notice the patterns that emerged.
And so this mistake was repeated throughout the numbers that were called.
Eventually, it was Norion’s turn.
He was one of the five geniuses, so everyone was eagerly looking forward to his win over those who had come before him.
All four who went before him—three managed to lift eight crystals, while one only lifted seven crystals—so Norion had to do better than them.
He tried, making sure his failure didn’t stop him from lifting less than eight crystals.
Thankfully, he managed to lift nine, albeit with sheer difficulty.
After him, Dorren went, and he also managed to lift nine, showing the rivalry wouldn’t let them relax when there was a slot to enter the flame tower on the line.
Madea followed and managed to lift nine crystals, even attempting the tenth, but she couldn’t.
Shaking her head, she walked away, and Elia went to see if she, too, was destined to be among the top five.
In the end, she also managed to lift nine crystals.
However, she wasn’t happy if one were to compare her achievement to those of Norion, Dorren, or Madea.
This meant that if Ostorious performed better than her, she would be the one to wash out, since there was no way Kent would fall behind any of them.
Kent had already lifted all ten crystals in the third trial, so she wasn’t banking on him to fail... so she could only hope Ostorious didn’t go beyond eight crystals.
Kent, of course, knew the outcome, but he just stood there as Ostorious’ turn came, and he walked to the glass chamber.
The moment Ostorious wrapped his energy around four crystals, Kent shook his head and smiled.
Queen Jascia, who was paying attention to Kent, narrowed her gaze as the realization dawned on her.
"I think with him here, even if for a few days, these kids will gain more experience than they could ever dream of." Naturally, she made up her mind to add to Kent’s punishment.
Ostorious managed to lift seven crystals, but that was when he felt the exhaustion reach deep down into his soul.
When he lifted the eighth, he couldn’t go beyond that, and knowing he had already failed, he dropped the crystals and left with a defeated smile.
The last person to walk into the chamber was Kent.
This time, he planned to show everyone that in the face of great strength and control, all planning is useless.
When he reached the glass chamber, he waved his hand, and his flame surged around all ten crystals.
Then, with ease, he lifted all the crystals from the glassy floor and suspended them ten inches above the ground.
"So he faked the first trial," Princess Elowen, who had managed to recover and return inside during the third trial, asked her mother as she gazed intently at Kent.
"He didn’t fake it...

He tried to show his fellow contestants something, but it seemed they failed to grasp it." Queen Elowen, who suspected Kent had discovered something about the trial, replied, already planning to know more.
"Why don’t you ask him, Mom?" Elowen said, but her mother smiled, "You can also ask him.
After all, you will be walking hand in hand with him soon."
Princess Elowen looked at her mother for a few seconds before the words she had forgotten came to mind: "Shameless."
Her mother just smiled before turning to Kent, who was walking off the stage.
"Kent Madson, I saw how you completed the third trial just a couple of minutes ago, and I would say it is completely different from how the fourth trial was completed.
Care to shed some light on that?"
Kent smiled, already expecting this when he felt the queen’s gaze on him.
He expected her to ask such a question, so he prepared a good yet short answer.
"The reason my third trial was different from the fourth was that I tried to show my fellow contestants how to lift all the crystals easily.
It turns out that the moment the crystals are six inches off the ground, their weight returns to normal, meaning the rune around the crystals is ineffective when the crystals are that high.
This also means instead of spending ten times the effort and energy to hold the crystals in the air, you only need one-tenth of the effort.
In other words, holding the crystals six inches off the ground would save you more energy to lift the remaining crystals."

chapters.title: Chapter 739: Next Plan [Bonus]
paragraphs: Hearing Kent’s answer, every last one—regardless of whether they were in the audience, the contestants, or the queen herself—was left stunned.
Never in their wildest dreams did they think something as simple as raising a crystal six inches off the ground would have such an effect in ways they never knew possible.
However, they knew it was possible because Kent had proved it. This then begged the question: what else did he know that could have helped everyone?

But nobody could blame him. Kent wasn’t obligated to tell them something he knew to be true. Of course, he told them, but they didn’t pay attention. Sometimes, it wasn’t always about hearing that could make a difference.
Sometimes, seeing could also make a difference.
Lord Yael appeared to congratulate all those who had won and give them their gifts...
"Congratulations, everyone. The four trials have tested all who qualified to participate, but in the end, only five will represent the Half-Elves at the opening of the Flame Tower.
I am proud of you all. As for your gifts, please come to the palace tomorrow. The queen has a few words for you and some bonuses that will prepare you for the Flame Tower.

As for those who couldn’t make it this year, keep training because in three years, your chance will come to enter. But for now, you will each receive a Mythic Grade Ambrosia apple and a 10,000-year-old Soul Cleanse Berry.
Know that with these two treasures in your hands, your future growth will be both smooth and terrifying, so don’t waste it."

He gave them their gifts and then looked at Kent. He gave him a slight nod before speaking, "The contestants who want their skills reviewed by Kent Madson can come to the palace tomorrow. Until then, thank you all for coming."
The moment Lord Yael finished his words, comments began to ring out. Kent looked in a certain direction and smiled, waving at three Half-Elves.

It was Arion, Cyran, and Helyra, the three Half-Elves he had saved on his way through the Flame Valley. Those who noticed this turned, and when they saw the three Half-Elves waving back, some became jealous.
Someone like Kent is the kind of person everyone would want to associate with. And seeing the three Half-Elves wave at him, they knew Kent shared some connection with them.
To make the three Half-Elves popular, Kent gestured for them to come, and after a few hesitations, they flew toward him.
"How are you three doing? I wanted to come look for you, but I was busy with something," Kent said, looking slightly happy.
And yes, he was happy because, while the Half-Elves accepted him as one of their own, the three could be said to be his friends.
At least he saw them as his friends.
"We are doing great," Arion, the leader of the three, said.
"Good to hear that. Were you able to become adventurers?" Kent asked, but they shook their heads.
"What happened? Were the flame spirits too weak?"
"No. The flame spirits would be more than enough to let us qualify to become adventurers. I was wondering if you might be interested in joining our team.
We know it is too much to ask, but we saw what you can do, and we believe joining us will be good for us, even if your stay here will be just a few weeks."
Kent smiled, hearing their request. It wasn’t unreasonable in any way. If anything, they wanted to use his help to cement their position in Elarion.
That is both brilliant and opportunistic.
However, sometimes one has to become opportunistic to achieve what one wants. Arion, Cyran, and Helyra were aware of this, and now they had made their request known.
Kent looked at them for a few seconds and nodded, "I don’t mind becoming an adventurer. I already planned on exploring this continent while I am here, so I might as well do that as an adventurer."
The three Half-Elves smiled happily. "Then we can go to the Adventurers Guild right now and register," Cyran proposed, and Kent nodded.
The competition was over, and everyone started leaving, so he had to go as well. He looked at Lord Yael and gave him a slight nod before walking away with the three Half-Elves.
"So those are the three friends he was talking about," King Thalirion said, watching Kent and the three soon-to-be adventurers walk away.
"Are they adventurers?" Queen Jascia asked, but the king shook his head.

He had already asked one of his elders to raise the status of Kent’s friends when he gave them the 1,000-year-old Soul Nourishing Berrys. However, after a quick investigation, the report he received wasn’t what he expected.

He expected the people Kent called friends to be among the most impressive adventurers in Elarion, but to think they weren’t even adventurers, nor had any of them refined their cores at least three times, he was taken aback.
However, he also knew he couldn’t choose who Kent took as friends, so for now, he was the elder to keep track of them and let him know.
After everyone left, the arena was closed for the time being. More competitions would be held, some of which would reward the hardworking individuals.

Kent gave them a lot they could offer their people, so they wanted to use every last thing they had to raise their standing in the world and also uplift the standard of living in Elarion to a more acceptable level.
Kent didn’t know if they had plans on how to handle the Elves, but he would leave that to the king and queen. He had already achieved his main objective for coming to Elarion.
Now, his next objective was to strengthen his Soul Flame to Tier 7. This meant he had to return to the Flame Valley, since he could grow both his Soul Flame and Flame Resistance there.

Though growing his Flame Resistance was no longer plausible just by walking in the Flame Valley, Kent had already discovered that the cores from his kills seemed to have some effect on it. So, he planned to hunt for cores and flame spirits.

chapters.title: Chapter 740: First Chess Piece, Moved [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Three days after the competition - Elvin Kingdom: Sylveria]
The looks of shock, anger, and jealousy painted the faces of the Elvin Queen and her elders like makeup. The past three days had been the worst for them and perhaps everyone.
It was as if one day they were on top, and the next second, they were at the bottom with no means or capability to ever rise back up again.
During the competition in Elarion, when Lord Yael announced the various rewards to be given to all participants, the spies hidden among the Half-Elves reported to their respective leaders.
The Elves were struck hard the moment they heard the unbelievable load of treasures the Half-Elves were giving away to mere warriors who hadn’t even reached the peak.
At first, they thought it was merely a bluff, but after the first round, when the 1,000-year-old Soul Cleansing Berry was given, they realized something wasn’t right.
Then the second round ended, and more reports came. After the third round, they knew things hadn’t been a bluff, that the Half-Elves truly had the means to give these rewards to their people.
What shocked them the most were the Spirit Grapefruit and the Ambrosia apple.
It struck them hard, making them realize soon that the Half-Elves would surpass them. And from what Lady Aelith and General Dalion had already said to them, the Elves started to panic.
It had been three days, but they still hadn’t come to terms with the news they got from their spies.
"From a 1,000-year-old Soul Cleansing Berry to a 10,000-year-old Spirit Grapefruit, then Ambrosia Apples, and if that wasn’t enough, they have to add a Tier 8 Innate Talent Awakening Pill.

I mean, what happened? What changed? What happened to the weaklings? We were buying them enough time before we took them down. How come they get to have all this, and even at this rate, have the means to surpass even us?"
Lord Arlen said, clenching his fist like a madman.
"Let’s not forget she is also back... their queen. I think I don’t have to point out what she is capable of," Lord Folwin added, looking even angrier than Lord Arlen.

"You don’t think they lied to us? We were there when Kenji attacked and saw her fall. So what happened? Had she recovered long ago and chosen to hide from everyone, planning and plotting for when she reveals herself?
I mean, look at the timeline: she woke up the day the human named Kent appeared.
That same day, he killed Kenji, the cause of her pain, and then a day later, they announced these ridiculous treasures that I don’t think even the Supreme Immortal sect will have a fraction of.
Where did they get them from?"
Queen Lunara sat calmly on her throne, but inwardly, she was seething.
While things could have been worse had the Half-Elves enticed the other races to aid them in attacking the Elves, the Half-Elves had become brilliant.

They spread the word throughout the entire world of their capabilities and where they stood now and then, announcing an alliance with the Bloodvein and inviting all races, including the Elves, to an auction in a month.
Things could have been worse, but now, it had become grim.
Queen Elanara knew deep within what the Half-Elves were doing. First, they would limit the quantity they had, then use conditions to sell the rest.

It would have been best if they sold everything at once, but the plan they’d devised would prevent the Elves from buying everything; they would pique everyone’s interest, then ensure everyone understood who was in charge.
The Half-Elves were winning, and soon, it would become clear to everyone.
"Lord Arlen, send people to Elarion. Tell them we would like to have a sit-down with them and talk things out," Queen Elanara said, and Lord Arlen nodded.
A few minutes later, five people, including Lord Arlen, left their kingdom and headed to Elarion, where they planned to carry out their queen’s orders.
Meanwhile, on the continents, when news of how the Half-Elves flaunted their wealth reached them, just like the Elves, they were shocked, wondering what had happened.
Then news of Kent Madson appearing in the Half-Elves’ kingdom also reached them, causing those in league with the Hand to start making plans to kill him.
However, that all changed when they again heard that Kent Madson had killed Kenji, popularly known as the Blade Whisperer.
They all realized things weren’t as simple as they thought. So they relaxed and sent spies to gather more info on him.

However, a few hours later, they received word that in a month, there would be an auction in the Half-Elves’ kingdom. This news came as a shock to them, considering some of the items they would allegedly sell there were truly out of this world.
So be it—the Dragons, the Elves, the Demons, the Beasts, or even the Dwarves—every last one of them had started preparing for the auction.
They, just like the Elves, looked down on the Half-Elves mainly because the Half-Elves have the blood of humans flowing through them.
To them, humans are at the bottom of the food chain, so they don’t place value on a race that has human blood flowing through them.
However, it now appears that the race they had looked down on now had the means to rule the world. This prompted them to start wondering if things were as simple as they seemed.
They would most definitely want to use this opportunity to establish and perhaps further develop the relationship they never had with the Half-Elves.
In the end, the goal was to obtain the treasures that the Half-Elves possess. The allure of having the resources of the Half-Elves would compel them to go the extra mile.
But then again, that was precisely what the Half-Elves were after.
They wanted them to get enticed, and when they reached the point of no return, the Half-Elves would let them know being part human isn’t exactly evil... after all, humans are natural schemers.

chapters.title: Chapter 741: Kent’s Dangerous but Brilliant Plan [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Elarion - Grand Jin Five Star Inn (VIP Private Room)]
It had already been five days since the competition.
The winners went to collect their gifts from the palace, as Lord Yael had instructed. However, instead of just the promised gifts, they walked away with more.

Of course, the Innate Talent Awakening Pill was made by Kent inside the tower, where time passed much faster than on the outside. In all, the winners walked away with the best treasures they could have ever dreamed of.
After that, Kent asked everyone to meet him at the Grand Jin Five-Star Inn in three days. That day was today.
Inside VIP Room 4, nine people were seated around a dining table, food served, but only one of them was eating.
That person, of course, was Kent, who, despite the tense atmosphere, remained unaffected. Arion, Cyran, and Helyra were there with him.
Norion, Madea, Elia, and Dorren were also seated, and the last person whose presence perhaps added to the tense atmosphere, Princess Elowen, was also there.
However, while her presence added to the tense atmosphere, it was more like watching Kent eat as if he were a beggar that left them tense.

They all expected him to be calm and collected, but the Kent they were seeing was easy-going and somewhat unruly. Of course, Arion, Cyran, and Helyra knew him better, but even so, they were a little taken aback.
"You know, I used to have this auntie... beautiful woman, puffy cheeks, and funny. She used to say those who don’t like food tend to grow lean to the point their bones become their flesh.
I don’t want that, and I know you all don’t want that, so why don’t you dig in? The food is rather delicious," Kent said, smiling at the eight gathered in the room with him.

They made subtle motions, and eventually, they started to eat. It was a silent meal that lasted for 30 minutes. When they were done, they all turned to Kent. After all, he was the one who had invited them.
"Very well, I called you here for no particular reason but to inform you of a plan I have cooked up to get you all up to standard before entering the Flame Tower.
Of course, my main reason for calling you here is not centered around the Flame Tower but the Supreme Immortal Sect.
Although not all of us will be entering the Flame Tower or the sect, this plan will ultimately bring about some significant changes in this kingdom."

Kent turned to Arion, Cyran, and Helyra and smiled. "As we discussed, within a year, I will become a core disciple, and then I can recommend you three. So that is why you are here... to train with the best of this kingdom."
The three nodded, but the rest, including the princess, raised their brows.
"You make it seem like becoming a core disciple is the easiest thing to do," Princess Elowen said, shaking her head.
She acknowledged that Kent was a monster, but hearing he planned to become a core disciple in no other place but the Supreme Immortal Sect, she couldn’t believe her ears.
Norion, Madea, Elia, and Dorren felt the same. They didn’t see that happening...
"The last person said to have reached the Core Disciple stage fastest was the Pill Princess, but it still took her 15 years," Norion added to what the princess said, which only made Kent smile.

"Well, I don’t plan on staying there for long, so a year is all I need to become a core disciple. Aside from that, why do you all think it’s impossible to become a core disciple in a year? I can become a core disciple at any time I choose.
When I am done with you all, becoming a core disciple won’t be something you have to fear. However, you will have to work for it, and it starts by handing over your soul flames."
"What do you mean by handing over our soul flames?" Dorren asked. "Without them, we wouldn’t even be able to enter the Flame Tower, much less comprehend a Flame Art."

"I know, but if you want to get into the Supreme Immortal Sect, then you will have to do as I say. First, the soul flame you have isn’t the real thing. It is a flame spirit, something meant to be fed to actual soul flames.
This means the ones you all have don’t possess the ability to devour other flames and gain their Aspect abilities.
This also means that before you can grow stronger, you must change your soul flames at some point, which, if you cannot, would mean your journey would come to an end.
However, by awakening your own soul flame, your growth is endless.

Let me make something clear: when it comes to the path of cultivation, reaching the peak of Core Formation isn’t even a quarter of the journey, so it will be best if you all free yourselves of this limitation now.
I will teach you a method to awaken your soul flame, and then, before the Flame Tower opens, we will head to the Flame Valley to hunt flame beasts in the core region.
This way, by the time the tower opens, every last one of you entering will come out smiling."
The room became quiet, everyone looking at Kent with varied expressions. What they had just heard was a brilliant plan, but as it turned out, it was dangerous—too dangerous to embark on.
What he said made sense. They knew there were limitations on their soul flames, so when they heard a fix, they couldn’t help but feel that this was the best thing that had happened to them.
"Can we really manually awaken our own soul flames?" Princess Elowen asked, and Kent nodded.
"You will be able to do it within a few days if you practice the method I will be giving you. That said, we should get started now, as it will take a couple of days to learn the method and apply it."
They all nodded and then began the retrieval process, where each of them handed over their soul flames to Kent. After devouring them, he felt his soul flame move closer to the Tier 7 stage.

chapters.title: Chapter 742: Second Floor - The Orphan War (1)
paragraphs: [Planet Killer Dungeon - First Floor: Middle Island]
Vexthra stood atop a large rock overlooking a vast expanse of seawater like the goddess she was. Beside her stood Neomi and Princess Lovina.

"Unity should be done with her training soon," Neomi commented, already looking toward what awaited them on the second floor. They had already spent close to a week on the first floor, so they wanted to move to the second floor.

However, with Unity training the secret archery technique they discovered on the middle island, they were forced to stay there much longer. Thankfully, a few hours later, Unity finished her training, and they were ready to get going.
The moment they were ready to move, Vexthra willed the tower, which opened a portal for them. They walked through it and, in the next second, appeared on a deserted battlefield, though not for long.

It was a vast expanse of battlefield, one that had witnessed horror, bloodshed, and carnage. Broken weapons lay strewn across the battlefield, and even though the battle had happened many years ago, the aura of death lingered.
Naturally, Neomi, Elaine, Velyra, and Lani felt at home. The death qi in the air filled them with strength. All four of them wanted to go crazy and slaughter.
However, aside from the aura of death, there was something else—something that made everyone feel a sense of injustice, as if something grim had happened on this battlefield before.
They felt the pain and loss, a feeling that drove them to want to know what had happened and put things right.
Meanwhile, Vexthra was busily reading the details of the second floor.
⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Floor Name: The Orphans War (2nd)⟧
⟦Power Level: Core Formation - Spirit Ascension (peak)⟧
⟦Description:
The first floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon is the battlefield of the Orphans. They fought for their place.
They fought without knowing their lineage. They fought for a sense of belonging, but in the end, it was all for nothing because they lost.
During the Althan war, the Orphans, tired of being suppressed by society, chose to fight back, and they did. However, the battle ended when they failed to bring down the three generals of carnage.⟧
Objective:

↠ You are the Orphans, children of the unknown. This war is yours, and under no circumstances should you fail. You must kill all soldiers and generals. Killing the general with the red eye patch is of great importance.
↠ The Orphans of Althan will never know peace until he is dead. The one who deals the finishing blow receives a special reward.
⟦Rewards⟧
↠ 1.2 Million Tower Points
↠ 1,900,000,000 Soul Essence
↠ Song of the Fallen
↠ Soul Lantern
↠ Bone Threads Tempering Elixir

⟦Note: All drops will be stored inside the Tower storage. Additionally, it is advisable to thoroughly explore the floors using the dungeon map, as there are hidden items that can only be discovered with detailed examination.
The map of the second floor will be activated after the floor has been cleared.⟧

Vexthra read the details and rewards with a calm expression. Kent made sure she had access to this aspect of the tower, so she was able to will a portal to open and even have access to the quest message.
"Gather around," Vexthra said, and everyone moved toward her.

"On this floor, we are merely orphans. Our role is to face the soldiers of Althan and kill them, including their three generals. According to the objective of this floor, we must kill the one with the red eye patch in the most painful way possible.
Lovina and Velyra will handle him. Remember, he must die screaming. For the rest of us, let’s ensure the dreams of the orphans are fulfilled.
I don’t know how, but the soldiers of Althan will now be facing us, so let’s make sure they don’t meet the next army since this will be their death."
Everyone smiled just as the temperature of the battlefield started to rise. They turned to the distance, and that was when they saw the mist coming.
From the mist came human soldiers charging forward with their swords, spears, axes, and other weapons drawn.
The sight would shake most armies, but those about to face these soldiers were already hungry for battle, so this was their moment to go crazy.
"I guess here we go again," Kaizo grinned, flexing his fist. He looked to his side and saw Unity already ready to get into action.
’There are three generals. Elaine and Velyra will be handling the floor boss, who is the general with the red eye patch. This means the other two generals are like mini floor bosses.
I need to get one of them before Unity steals them from me again,’ Kaizo thought, and then he moved. Naturally, everyone already expected this, so when he moved, they followed.
[Thunderblast Clap]

Kaizo used one of his many skills to land the starting blow, blasting the battlefield with devastating consequences; however, instead of his clap affecting everyone, which in this case, his teammates, it was aimed at the soldiers of Althan.
A few died on the spot, while some were thrown into the air. However, they never landed since before they could even fully rise, arrows flashed out, taking them down.

Unity moved through the air, aiming her bow at a few soldiers who managed to evade Kaizo’s opening attack. At the same time, a wave of mind attack washed over the battlefield, striking the soldiers of Althan.
Zaila made her move and backed away, leaving the rest to her sisters.
Most of the soldiers lost their balance, allowing Selene and Val to make their move. The two swordwomen moved with the wind and unleashed dozens of sword slashes within seconds.

Selene was using the lunar energy flowing through her body, just as Val was doing. There was no moon up in the sky; however, their primordial spaces have many moons, so they weren’t running out of energy anytime soon.
But they weren’t the only ones having fun; Neomi was also moving like the angel of death. Wherever she moved, death and destruction trailed her.
Vexthra was at the back watching them with a calm expression. Since she was their leader and trainer, she observed them to identify areas where they were lacking, so she could help them later.

"Their limit is not in sight." After watching them for a while, she smirked. Thinking they would have a hard time on the second floor was her looking for an excuse to strengthen their foundations further.
However, so far, she had seen nothing worth noting.
Just like that, they ensured the soldiers’ numbers thinned out and gradually decreased, until only a few hundred remained.
A few among the soldiers were already at the Spirit Ascension stage; however, they weren’t having much of a field day like they had expected.
However, when two soldiers clad in much darker armor appeared, everyone felt the overwhelming presence of their aura. They are much more dangerous than the ones they had killed.

chapters.title: Chapter 743: Second Floor - The Orphans War (2)
paragraphs: "I will take the one wielding the axe; you can have the other," Kaizo said to Unity, who smiled back at him as the two soldiers appeared.
They were both clad in dark armor, but one wielded a spear and the other an axe. Naturally, Kaizo was after the one wielding the axe because he knew they were both brutes.
"Fine," Unity said, knowing that if she were to become unruly this time, Kaizo would actually lose his mind. So she took the one wielding the spear and started firing arrows at him.
Kaizo charged at the one wielding the axe, unleashing a powerful punch that created a sonic boom in his wake, shaking the very ground before landing on the axe of the brute general.
He crossed his arms over his chest just as Kaizo’s fist landed. It created a powerful impact, one that sent the general skidding back.
However, instead of flying away, he came to a halt after moving back three meters. Kaizo grinned.
"Looks like this one is much more powerful than the Spirit Ascension beasts on the first floor."
Unity had the same thought when she saw how the spear general was evading and blocking her arrows. Every shot was blocked or evaded.
However, instead of feeling afraid or angry, Unity felt some excitement, just like Kaizo, who also felt this would be a good warm-up.
So they started getting fiercer.

Kaizo began moving much faster, punching with greater force. In response, the general launched an even more aggressive attack and blockade. However, from a distance, Vexthra saw that it was only a matter of time before the two generals met their end.
She saw Kaizo wasn’t even trying.
His strength was robust, and his foundation was firm, so facing someone who hadn’t even had a chance to land an attack on him yet said it all.
Of course, it wasn’t like Kent hadn’t made sure of that.

He ensured that the materials used to upgrade his undead were of the highest value. This way, after their upgrade, not only would their foundations be untouched, but when it came down to sheer strength, they would be unlike anything else.
Kaizo, Vaelros, Zareth, and Sylara were all impressive in their own right.
So Kaizo wouldn’t even face any threat if dozens of these generals attacked him. He slowly kept pushing the general back.
Unity was the same.
Meanwhile, with people like Neomi, Velyra, and the rest handling the main soldiers, the battle was almost over.

Unity toyed with the general for a couple of minutes before taking out one of the arrows Alina had modified with her arrays. The arrows were already deadly, but with Alina’s modification, they became something else.
She activated no skill or bow enhancement. However, when the arrow entered her bow and she pulled on the bowstring, she felt something that caused her to look back at Alina, who was grinning at her.
Unity wondered what Alina was doing when she added these arrays to the arrows.
However, instead of dwelling on that, she released the bowstring, causing the arrow to flash out of her bow, appearing behind the head of the general.
The arrow went through his head before he even realized it.
It was instantaneous.
At the same time, Kaizo also had had enough. He channeled lightning into his palm and used a movement skill that let him get closer to the general before landing a palm strike on his chest.
The lightning Kaizo gathered on his palm exploded, rupturing the organs in the general’s body.
It would have been agonizing if Kaizo hadn’t done it right, but his [Divine Brute Palm Strike] skill is meant to kill instantly.
Just one clean attack and all organs will be destroyed. So Kaizo used it and the general couldn’t block it...
Right when the second general appeared, the floor boss came, looking imposing.
He held a club in his hands, stood almost three meters tall, and was clad in an even darker shade of metallic armor.
He had a red eye patch, dark hair, and the aura emanating from him was peak Ascendant, but stronger than the two Kaizo and Unity had killed.
"Let’s go," Velyra said, and Princess Lovina nodded. They moved, and soon they were closer to the red-patch general.
Princess Lovina formed an orb in her palm and threw it at the red-patch general, who swung his club, shattering the orb instantly.
It was one quick swing that shattered the orb, but it was his fault for choosing to smash it.
The moment he did, he felt it—a fiery burn, one that couldn’t be ignored—enter his body, burning deep within.
His skin remained unchanged; there was no external burn whatsoever. However, on the inside, the burn was too much, causing the general to drop his club and start screaming.
"Did I go too far?" Princess Lovina asked Velyra, who shook her head, smiling. Anything that is poisonous is considered excessive.
Velyra wanted to start the torture early, so she moved, executing a series of sword swings that immediately landed on the general, drawing blood.
Velyra moved back and looked at Lovina. "Handle the rest. And make sure he suffers like big sister said."
Lovina nodded and extended her palm.
Thousands of orbs appeared and then transformed into green wasps. They moved through the cut marks Velyra had created and entered the general’s body, starting to eat him from the inside.
His painful cries were so loud that Veera, the dreadful necromancer, who was planning on taking this floor boss as her undead, changed her mind.
"He will be too traumatized even in death, so he is worthless."
And she wasn’t wrong; what was happening to the Red Eye Patch General wasn’t simple. If anything, it was just too evil.
Velyra created the cut marks, drawing blood, so she could use her blood manipulation skills to keep healing the general, while Lovina used the poison wasps to torment him from the inside.
If it were only Princess Lovina, the general would have died within a few seconds, but thanks to Velyra, he had been screaming for ten minutes already.
After a while, Vexthra told them to end it.
Velyra deactivated her skill, and Lovina snapped her fingers, turning the general into a husk. His body deflated, meaning the wasps had consumed every last organ in his body.
It was a horrifying sight, but the ladies and the legion didn’t seem to care.
Vexthra received the Quest completed notice, making her smile. The quest ended faster than she had expected.
They quickly began searching for new clues while Vexthra reported to Kent, who was riding a carriage with the eight half-elves, en route to the Flame Valley.

It would have been agonizing if Kaizo hadn’t done it right, but his [Divine Brute Palm Strike] skill is meant to kill instantly.
Just one clean attack and all organs will be destroyed.
So Kaizo used it and the general couldn’t block it...
Right when the second general appeared, the floor boss came, looking imposing.
He held a club in his hands, stood almost three meters tall, and was clad in an even darker shade of metallic armor.
He had a red eye patch, dark hair, and the aura emanating from him was peak Ascendant, but stronger than the two Kaizo and Unity had killed.
"Let’s go," Velyra said, and Princess Lovina nodded.
They moved, and soon they were closer to the red-patch general.
Princess Lovina formed an orb in her palm and threw it at the red-patch general, who swung his club, shattering the orb instantly.
It was one quick swing that shattered the orb, but it was his fault for choosing to smash it.
The moment he did, he felt it—a fiery burn, one that couldn’t be ignored—enter his body, burning deep within.
His skin remained unchanged; there was no external burn whatsoever.
However, on the inside, the burn was too much, causing the general to drop his club and start screaming.
"Did I go too far?" Princess Lovina asked Velyra, who shook her head, smiling.
Anything that is poisonous is considered excessive.
Velyra wanted to start the torture early, so she moved, executing a series of sword swings that immediately landed on the general, drawing blood.
Velyra moved back and looked at Lovina.
"Handle the rest.
And make sure he suffers like big sister said."
Lovina nodded and extended her palm.
Thousands of orbs appeared and then transformed into green wasps.
They moved through the cut marks Velyra had created and entered the general’s body, starting to eat him from the inside.
His painful cries were so loud that Veera, the dreadful necromancer, who was planning on taking this floor boss as her undead, changed her mind.
"He will be too traumatized even in death, so he is worthless."
And she wasn’t wrong; what was happening to the Red Eye Patch General wasn’t simple.
If anything, it was just too evil.
Velyra created the cut marks, drawing blood, so she could use her blood manipulation skills to keep healing the general, while Lovina used the poison wasps to torment him from the inside.
If it were only Princess Lovina, the general would have died within a few seconds, but thanks to Velyra, he had been screaming for ten minutes already.
After a while, Vexthra told them to end it.
Velyra deactivated her skill, and Lovina snapped her fingers, turning the general into a husk.
His body deflated, meaning the wasps had consumed every last organ in his body.
It was a horrifying sight, but the ladies and the legion didn’t seem to care.
Vexthra received the Quest completed notice, making her smile.
The quest ended faster than she had expected.
They quickly began searching for new clues while Vexthra reported to Kent, who was riding a carriage with the eight half-elves, en route to the Flame Valley.

chapters.title: Chapter 744: Aftermath [Bonus]
paragraphs: [Is it already done?]
Kent asked when he felt his connection to Vexthra activate.
"Yes. The battle lasted only 24 minutes," Vexthra responded.
[I see. Then, I suppose the first five floors will be manageable for them. I don’t think they will need my help.] Kent said, and Vexthra nodded.

"I think so, too. None of them is using their trump cards yet, so I guess the first five floors will be manageable. However, unless they bring out their game from the 6th floor upwards, I don’t suppose they will have it easy this time around."

[We can never know until they get there. Thankfully, we have 12 years to clear all floors, so we still have time. However, I also have to get to a high world quickly so that they can start raising their cultivation bases again.]
Vexthra couldn’t deny that. However, she knew Kent had some missions yet to finish in this world before he could leave.
For now, she would help her sisters and the legion move sturdily so that reducing Kent’s workload would be accomplished as planned.
"We are about to explore the second floor since the map has activated."
[Good. What about the drops, are they still only memory keys?] Kent asked.

"Not exactly. This time, Alina, Mara, and Skoggr got a drop, which gave them a memory key. But aside from that, Lovina also received a drop, but instead of a key, she got a skill manual that once belonged to her past self, I suppose.
It was something she received from dealing the last blow to the floor boss."
Kent smiled inwardly. He had yet to awaken Princess Lovina’s true name, so hearing she had already started receiving stuff from her past life made him happy.
[I will awaken her true name when I come back from the Flame Valley. By then, I am sure they will all start seeing the true nature of the dungeon and its dangers.]
"That will be great for her. She will finally be able to regress her primordial spirit and start walking the ancient path just like all of us."
After a few more talks, Kent cut the connection.
Vexthra made sure every last one of them got the bone thread tempering elixir, which immediately boosted their strength to another level before going about their search.
The map was becoming more detailed, so they started to find clues and hidden messages a few minutes into the search.
Meanwhile, Kent first took a look at the descriptions of the two items, aside from the elixir, soul essence, and tower points he received.
The first is [Song Of The Fallen].

It is a soul-hunting song that can be played with any instrument. It has seven verses, and judging by the requirements to play such a song, Kent knew it would be a while before such a melody was heard on battlefields.
He felt no attachment to it, almost as if it wasn’t meant to be his. So he knew the Tower storage would be the best place for it for the time being.
The second, however, was something he could use.
[Soul Lantern]

According to the description, this lantern allows him to catch the soul spirits of those he has slain, or any soul around him or the lantern. He doesn’t know how far it extends, but he knows the lantern is a broken item.
Having the ability to capture soul spirits is awesome.
However, it goes beyond that. The description of this lantern also indicates that it allows him to convert soul spirits into soul essence.
Souls, when the main body dies, come in three forms.
The first is the Soul Essence.
That is what Kent devours after every kill using the automated Soul Devour skill. This is the purest form of every soul, and almost everyone who devours souls goes after this one.
The second is the Soul Spirit.

This version is the one that can be absorbed into the soul flags to create restrictions, whether for defense or attack. These soul spirits can’t be absorbed because the essence that keeps them is much more lethal.
It was one of the reasons why Nykali was able to create spectrals from them. Soul spirits aren’t tamed like soul essence. Soul spirits can be weaponized to become spectrals.
However, now this lantern can convert them into soul essence, which he can consume.
As for the last form, it is the Damned Spirits. These ones go straight to the underworld, where they become dead spirits, meant to remain there forever.
Naturally, Kent knew those couldn’t be absorbed, regardless of how monstrous one was. Yama wouldn’t allow that. But soul spirits are a different matter.
And now, he has acquired something he can use to expand his soul universe further. The best part: he doesn’t even have to take it out to absorb souls.
By activating it, a tattoo of a lantern appears on his arm, which, whenever there is a soul, he can easily absorb as if it were the most normal thing to do.

’This is a good one. I can finally earn not just from absorbing the essence, but also the spirit.’ Kent entered his soul universe for a moment, and what he saw brought a smile to his face, making the eight Half-Elves within the carriage wonder what was funny.
The asteroid is coming along steadily.

It has now grown to the size of an adult head, and the energy he felt from it was enough to tell him that when it is unleashed, the unfortunate soul that this asteroid will strike will scream its way to the underworld.
’I need to add more races to my Guardian Tower so that I can create more of this. If I were to unleash this one now, I would have to start a new asteroid from scratch.
However, if I add more races to my Guardian Tower, creating other things should be sufficient. I need to have at least ten stadium-sized asteroids before ascending to a high world.

Under no circumstances should I lack even when facing an immortal.’ Kent made his plan, so he sent the lantern to Vexthra for now to use in capturing the souls they would claim from the third floor upward.
Kent, on the other hand, is now looking to strengthen his soul flame, as he will be entering the Flame Tower in two weeks, and a week after that, the sect...
